title: Stylish airport travel bag with great features
text:
I can't say how long I've been searching for the right airport bag that won't weigh me down and gives me the autonomy to carry more stuff without having to choose between my messenger bag and a larger briefcase. I'm pretty stoked to have finally found a briefcase that matches my criteria and delivers the most features I've seen out of something this stylish. I had people compliment my bag while waiting for my flight.

The best feature is that it comes with a luggage strap. I can't say how much it's helped to have to just leave the bag on my carry-on roller and not worry about lugging it around.

In this bad boy I can fit two laptops, all my chargers and two 1" binders with plenty of room to spare. The weight on this bag is a big considerable, but nothing that stops me from considering adding extra weight to it if need be. The bottom of the bag has a rounded trim that gives it solid construction and protects the bag from incidental contact. The very bottom has 4 brass feet that allow the bag to stand. So if ever you separate from your bag and want to keep it as a standalone, it will be able to stay upright. The bag is pretty balanced, so I didn't really have a problem with weight distribution.

This bag takes perfect features from the other Polare bags - like the front pockets (4 of them) - and puts them behind a zipper which is great. They do puff up a bit if over stuffed, but I keep smaller items in those pockets so it doesn't look like it's about to burst. The bag also comes with a secret back pocket that I use to keep my important documents, phone and things I need to reach quickly.

I don't know about the original version, but I do know I've brought up the lack of quality on the liner and interior components before to Polare. So, as far as the updated version goes, it looks like a huge improvement from what I saw on prior reviews. The elastic on the luggage strap and laptop hold-down is great. They reinforced the Velcro on the inside so it doesn't get worn out easily. They kept the same leather tab on the inside to protect items from getting scratched on the zipper. This is a very intentional design and excellent construction. As always, incredibly happy with my bag and will continue supporting this amazing company.

title: Working from home? Quiet and quality
text:
Working from home more often got me to think about upgrading my home office setup. I bought this full size keyboard and mouse because I wanted quiet keys that wouldn't wake up the family when I work late. This combo fit the bill perfectly. I can't speak to the long term durability of this kit because I only recently received it. That said, this is my review after 1 full week of working with it 8-10 hours/day. The keyboard is as promised: Quiet, svelt yet full size. The keys are quieter than my Logitech wireless compact keyboard and I can easily work while folks around me are sleeping. No loud clicky clacky sound yet there is certainly positive feedback on each press and the buttons do not feel squishy. It has everything you would expect from a full size keyboard including audio and internet browser controls and lights indicating number lock, caps lock, and low battery. Lightweight but not cheap feeling. My one con about the keyboard is that the height is not adjustable. I have not found that to be a problem for me as the keyboard is at a comfortable angle and height for me to work all day on it.

As for the mouse, it is smooth scrolling and the buttons - like the keyboard - are whisper quiet. It does not have DPS adjustability but you can, of course, adjust the speed in your system settings on Windows. It's really not a big deal. I guess if you want a super fancy gaming mouse you would pass on this but for the rest of us who use their computer to get work done, this mouse fits the bill.

I would recommend this combo keyboard and mouse for anyone who wants a wireless full size keyboard but doesn't want a loud clicky clacky sound but still requires positive feedback on each press. Perfect for working from home or anywhere where sound may be an issue.

title: NOT like the original
text:
Pro audio guy here, many people say these are just as good as the original, they are not. I do appreciate their effort, however, and hope to seem them updated to a true alternative. The Senn's are way too expensive.

They are much easier to install than the Senn's too so that's nice (though it may be part of why they aren't as good in terms of sound).

LAMY version - hotter on the ears than the original, foam is too stiff so the driver sits further away from the ear changing the sound of the headphones (less mids - what the 380 is all about and critical for analytical listening), less sound isolation (of outside noise) than the original, less comfortable, smaller (difficult to get headphones into original case) but half the price.

VELVET/BLACK version - Terrible. Unless isolation of outside noise is absolutely not a concern I would stay away from these. They have as much isolation as my broken Sennheiser pads did. The comfort was better, the sound issue was the same as the LAMY, they didn't sit at the right distance from the ear, same size issue, easy to install, blocked almost zero outside noise.

If you use your 380's for anything professional or critical get the original pads. If the sound signature shifting a bit isn't important to you, a slightly smaller size/case problems doesn't matter, and outside isolation isn't a factor, then you could save some money here.

title: Not worth the money
text:
I bought this expecting that I would get somewhere near the advertised speed for writes, but instead this drive performed like a below average drive costing about 1/3 as much as what this drive does.

It's HUGE and heavy. It seems like it would be heavy duty and built for fast writes. I have drives that are about half the size of this that perform far better.

So this is what I did. I started using this in a Linux system (Ubuntu 19.10) and I noticed the write speed to this drive started out around 300MB/s which I was very happy about. I was writing a 90GB file to the USB drive from an SSD, so there was plenty of speed from the read device to sustain a high speed of writing, after writing out a few GB however, the drive started to slow down. By the time the write op was finished the speed was showing about 60MB/s. Under Ubuntu the progress bar shows an average speed, so that was the average over 90GB being written to the drive. I then took the drive to a Win7 machine. After writing the file that I copied to the drive, I wanted to see what would happen on that machine, so I copied the same 90GB file again to the USB drive. The same behavior happened. After writing maybe 15GB of data to the drive, the progress bar in Win7 started to show the speed gradually dropping down. Once again, under Win7, the progress bar is an average write speed over the time of the write op. By the time the the write was finished, the progress bar was showing data being written at about 50MB/s. Once again that is the average write speed over the entire write op. This is typical that my read/write speeds are slower on Windows than Linux. My wife has a machine with Win8.1 on it, so I decided to test it there to watch the progress bar, because on Win8.1 it shows the actual write speed at any given moment, not an average. I assumed that after writing 10 - 15GB of data I was going to see a quick drop off in the write speed, and that's exactly what happened. The write speed dropped from around 200MB/s to between 25 - 40MB/s, and the write speed stayed in that low range the rest of the time the file was being written to this drive.

There are basically two things that can explain that behavior. One is the drive is defective. Well, at $80 USD for a 256GB drive I expect it to work. That's a really high price for that amount of capacity (256GB). The other thing that explains that behavior is the memory just isn't very fast, and the drive has a built in cache the same way SSDs do and many other devices that allows you to write a small amount of data to the device at very high speeds, but once the cache is full, you have to write straight to the main storage of the device and you are now writing at whatever speed that storage is capable of.

Now, I don't know which of these is the case. I returned the drive because if I get a bad one the first time and it's the most expensive USB drive I've ever bought, I have no faith in getting another one.

What I do know is I have 2 other brands of USB drives at the capacity I bought. For one of those, the older ones I bought would maintain a write speed of around 150MB/s. The newer ones unfortunately aren't as fast (and why I was looking to buy something else), and they only maintain a write speed of 100MB/s. Then I have another brand and it will maintain write speeds of 80 - 90MB/s. This drive was only maintaining a write speed of around 50MB/s, and from what Win8.1 was showing, without that initial burst of speed, it was only writing 25 - 40MB/s. That's simply terrible for a drive that's supposed to write at around 400MB/s.

title: Well worth it.
text:
In a nutshell, this item worked just fine. Fit was fantastic and the price is well less than half the name-brand.

Details:
Before purchasing I read the complaints that it was flimsy and breakable. I wear my GoPro hiking, so generally it's not at a huge risk of being destroyed if a mount breaks. I figured this item was worth trying out. When I unpacked it, it didn't seem flimsy to me although I admit I didn't put it through any torture tests.

I've been using the GoPro magnetic swivel clip, clipped onto my backpack strap up until now. The trouble with that is that it moves around quite a bit, usually changing the angle of the camera to the ground. No matter how often I check and correct it, I get home to find most of my pictures at an angle (not zero) to optimum. I hoped the chest mount would keep the camera level to the ground without so much checking and adjusting. As you might expect, it did wonderfully at that.

The size of the harness is barely suitable for me. If I had my druthers, they'd offer an "extra large," but they don't. I'm 6'1" and 235#. I wore it with the harness straps fully extended - the biggest they can be. It was not uncomfortable, but I'm staying away from Christmas cookies for the next 11 months. I wore it under my jacket but over my shirt. I'm pretty sure it would not go outside my jacket. Definitely not comfortably.

When wearing it, it again felt sturdy enough. I think I'd use it even skydiving, bungee jumping or motorcycling. Checking camera functions was much easier with the chest mount than the swivel clip. I could easily flip the camera forward and check battery life, etc., then flip it back into place and move on. With the swivel clip, I had to take it off to check camera status, then put it back on and re-orient it.

In all, I think this mount is just fine. For less than half the price of the brand-name mount, it's pretty easy to recommend.

title: Getting 2104 errors and an unusable SSD. This is common with Crucial m.2 SSDs and Lenovo laptops.
text:
I bought this SSD after reading the reviews and what Crucial says on its website that their P1 m.2 2280 1TB SSD is compatible with the Lenovo Thinkpad X1 Extreme. It was an excellent price point at $119, and the reviews I read on Amazon warranted my purchase. Even with one review saying that it wasn't compatible with the X1 Extreme, I decided to purchase the P1 anyway, maybe thinking that the reviewer got a bad SSD. Within a week, however, I'm getting the error, "2104 detection error on ssd2 m.2" when restarting my computer. I open up Windows Explorer only to see the P1 is no longer showing up. I decided to reseat the P1 into my laptop, hoping that the SSD was not seated correctly in the m.2 slot and was the reasons for that error. The SSD worked for another week, but when placing my laptop to sleep, the P1 would disappear, only reappearing when I restart my computer. Today, it disappeared again. When I restarted my laptop, the "2104 detection error on ssd2 m.2" error disappeared. I had to reseat the P1 again to get access to it. The only good thing about this is that all my data was not corrupt and was able to be moved to one of my external hard drives.

Doing more research on the internet (which I should have done before the purchase--instead I listened to Crucial's website), I found out visiting Lenovo's forums that this error is widespread with Lenovo laptops and the m.2 SSDs of Crucial without any fix. It seems that the only proven aftermarket SSDs that work with Lenovo laptops is Samsung and Toshiba, being that these two SSDs are what is already being put in stock laptops. I know this issue is partially Lenovo's fault, but Crucial has its website claiming that the P1 is fully compatible with my Thinkpad X1 Extreme. The P1 definitely isn't compatible. I hope that this review helps people with Lenovo laptops when purchasing the Crucial P1 1TB SSD.

title: 3 month usage review
text:
Environment:
Have a 30x14 home theatre with overhead projector mount throwing to a 110” screen. The mount is slightly behind the front row viewers head.

Installation:
Easy as they come. I had a HT2050 and did a direct drop and replace with this unit. Contrary to some reviewers, I actually like the white housing as it blends in better with the white ceiling. Power and an HDMI input from the receiver and we were up and running.

Gaming:
We play fortnite on this setup primarily and this is where the 16ms lag time shines. There is virtually no perceived lag or effect on gameplay. Running and gunning on a 110” screen has been the hit of the neighborhood. Colors look great and there’s no issues.

Movies:
I have found that the HT2050 I had produces a slightly better black image. The quality at 1080p is still great and crisp.

Gripes:
Lots of people complain about the fan noise and it’s a little muffled being up high against the ceiling versus on a table in front of the viewer but it is still a little noticeable. For this price point i wish they had put a quieter fan in.

Also, despite being able to download and remotely load firmware updates and color profiles that has been more of a nice to have and Viewsonic really hasn’t put out any firmware updates.

Major selling points:
The RGBRGB wheel is a must in these projectors and i was happy to see that included in this projector. Ive also enjoyed the backlit remote as my Sony remote isn’t backlit and you have to fumble a little bit with that one.

text: The only complaint is the instructions don't give you all the information you need. There is no explanation for the red leads that are at each end of the RCA video cable, they aren't even shown in the schematic.  You get a short lead with a red wire for the reverse circuit and a black wire for ground that will power the camera when in reverse. The RCA video cable connects to your display in the vehicle cabin. The red lead on the RCA cable can be used to connect to a reverse trigger  on your head unit that would activate the backup camera mode when you shift into reverse. Splice this into the reverse lamp circuit at the rear and the other end to the trigger wire on the head unit. It could also be used to power the camera. The camera itself and bracket do not have a top or up indication on them so you will have to get assistance to have the video level and properly orientated. It would be helpful if they had a tab up indication on the camera body. It is a very clear feed and you get the option to use the programmed guidelines or if you don't want them or have a display that gives you the option to calibrate your own, you can just cut the white wire loop on the camera lead. (Make sure you tape it off) It took a while to get the unit orientated and aimed properly, it was worth it. Mine is connected to a Boss Audio BVC9685A in a 2012 Mazda 3s

title: Not a bad camera bag but not great either.
text:
I'll start with the feedback about the Mirrorless Mover series in general:
They're mostly just lightly padded boxes with a basic three-sided zippered top (that opens towards you - not away from you) and one pocket on the interior of the top panel. The front zippered pocket does not expand and houses the removable waterproof cover (in smaller cases the waterproof cover takes up most or all of the front pocket). There is one or two non-expanding slip pockets inside the front zippered pocket. Most of the bags in this series are generally compact and lightweight (with the exception of the "i" series, which is noticeably heavier). These Mirrorless Mover bags are still too big for my Canon M100 - specifically too tall and too deep causing extra space that everything is moving around. Unfortunately this is a common problem I'm finding with all bags - they really are not optimized for a compact mirrorless.

That's the basics. Now here's what I don't like about this series:
1. The magnetic flap. It's big, in the way, annoying and completely unnecessary. ThinkTank claims it's there for quick access but it mostly hinders any access to the main cargo area with its mass of floppy fabric.
2. The zippers are not very smooth and are difficult around the corners.
3. The strap is small and not very comfortable plus it connects with metal spring clips onto metal D-rings making for a noisy bag.

Now, specifically for the Mirrorless Mover 20 - this one probably fills my size requirements best of all of the Mirrorless Mover Series (I've tried the 5, 10, 20 and 25i). The 20 fit my Canon M100 with a 15-45mm, 24mm macro and 22mm pancake with room to spare. The front pocket is still slim enough to be impractical and the strap is not overly comfortable. And then there is that dumb magnetic flap, which is annoying enough for me to return the bag.

title: The most extensive set of electronics repair tools I've seen. Terrific value
text:
OK, so I have several of these mega-bit collections of repair tools now: One for home, one for the repair kit, one for work. These things are amazing, featuring 100 or more driver bits--enough so that no matter what electronics device you're trying to open (and no matter what ridiculous non-standard bit head they've decided to use), you can probably get it open.

If you have ever tried to open a phone or a laptop or a shaver or whatever, you know that manufacturers use non-standard fasteners to keep prying hands out. So you NEED a kit like this. And if you don't have one...well, you're looking at this listing on Amazon, aren't you?

All right. So in the past few years, an endless number of suppliers have come out with zillion-bit sets. The first one I bought had around 50 bits, and I thought that was the cat's meow at the time. But now, the standard is more around 100 bits. This particular kit has 101 bits, and that's more than enough. It also includes a driver to hold the bits, extensions, converters to allow you to use the bits in an electric drill (but, please, DON'T do that--you don't want to use that kind of torque with these bits--hand torque only). If this kit only had the bits, it would be nice.

But what really sets this kit apart is all the other stuff, aside from the bits. It includes a LOT of tools useful for prying part electronics parts (e.g. the screen on a phone or laptop, the casing for an external hard drive, etc.) These include both a large variety of tools to aid in the prying and also a bunch of picks that can be used to keep the parts apart once you separated them. If you have ever watched any of the videos on the repair sites, the first thing they'll tell you is that you need a set of tools to help pull things apart. Many of these kits have some, but this kit has more than any other kit I've seen.

You also get various tools like a suction cup to pull a screen off without prying, a pin to remove the SIM card from your phone, several tweezers, an air puffer, a ruler, a magnetic mat to hold loose screws, a bit magnetizer/demagnetizer, etc.

All the non-bit stuff forms a very substantial kit in and of itself and one that you would want to have around the house, as well.

So you should really look at this as two kits: The bits, and the prying/removal kit.

It all wraps up in a velcro release roll-up (see photos). The bits are in their own hardshell plastic case. This is preferable to some of these kits, which put the bits into holders in the velcro roll--where they can fall out. Personally, I am keeping the bit case separate from the rest of the stuff, and use the velcro roll for all the prying/etc. tools.

On the whole, you may be thinking this is more kit than you need, and maybe you can save a few bucks by focusing on a kit with just the bits. But, trust me, eventually, you'll be happy--maybe thrilled--that you splurged a few bucks on the whole kit'n'kaboodle. This is the kind of thing you don't need until you do, and when you do need it, you'll be so glad you have it and don't have to put your urgent project aside until you can "get the right tools".

title: These speakers have a slot on the back for wall mounting, no other accessories necessary.
text:
I bought a pair of these Atmos/height speakers a year and a half ago and placed them on top of a pair of Klipsch floor speakers pointing up toward the ceiling to achieve the reflective sounds bouncing off the ceiling back down at me. Don’t bother doing this with any Atmos speaker. Any audio expert will tell you trying to bounce sound off the ceiling back down to the listening area is a crappy experience. So I mounted them on the wall near the ceiling thus them pointing down at me and it’s a world of difference. So recently I decided to finally buy another set for the rear, again mounting them near the ceiling pointing directly down at the listening area.

If one set is good, two sets of these speakers sounds amazing. The sound effects were great watching Mission Impossible Fallout. At the end of the movie during the helicopter chase scene, the chopper blades literally sounded like they was right above my head. Very impressive!

In general, Klipsch makes quality speakers and my entire 9.1 surround sound system, minus the SVS subwoofer, are by Klipsch powered by a Marantz SR7011 AVR. I have these Atmos/height speakers crossover set at 100hz although I’m pretty sure you can set them at 80hz which is Dolby THX standard. Klipsch claims these are full range speakers.

Personally I would only run these as Atmos/height speakers for ambient sounds. I’ve heard some people use them as regular surround speakers but I wouldn’t use them in that capacity. I prefer speakers with a more dynamic frequency range for surround speakers.

I would recommend these to others, they are reasonably priced at $300 as of this review. If you place these in a proper location and calibrate them correctly via your AVR, you’ll get great sound quality out of these speakers.

title: Robust portable laptop
text:
I have used the Razer Blade Stealth for over a Month now and think it is awesome.
It is extremely light and portable, but it also has a dedicated graphics core.

Before I had a 14 inch gaming laptop that while very good, I always left at home.
It weighted over 4lbs and the battery did not last very long.
But as someone who really travels a lot, the laptop at home was kind of useless.

Not the Razer Blade Stealth. It is so light, that I carry it around with me all the time and forget that it is there.
If I then sit down for a coffee I can pull out this sleek little thing at any time.
And it is still strong enough for me to get game development work done.

Note that this laptop fills a very small niche.
If you want a strong gaming laptop, you can get better ones for the same price. Even from the same company (Razer). But they are much bigger and the battery life is very bad.
If you want a ultra-book with long battery life, again, you can buy a better one for the same price.
But an ultra-book can not handle any 3D stuff at all.
The Razer Blade Stealth is the perfect fit in between those too.
For me, I am traveling a lot and this is my secondary machine besides a very strong desktop at home.
So think about what it is you need.

I have two small issues, but they are very minor:
1. The power button is right next to the delete key. I needed some time to get used to that.
2. The power supply is very small and light, this is great, but if you are running heavy 3D stuff, the battery does not really charge much at the same time. For me that is still OK, because I am happy about the very light power supply.

title: Barely Passable!
text:
Let's be clear here, we are reviewing a TV that costs well over $1,000. Yet so many people are not holding it to that standard. Wait until Black Friday. This television does a lot right, but for the money it is not worth it. The X950G has blooming that destroys dark room viewing, unless you dim your tv substantially(Which greatly darkens the image, more than normal, especiallyin cinema mode.), and while the overall picture may be pretty fantastic, it's still not beating TVs from 2017 like the X900E, which this was going to replace.

What's worse, is that Sony still forces you to accept Google terms of service, before even allowing you to use the product you just paid out all this money for. I don't know about you but I don't like to be forced into submit before, I'm even able to use the product I just invested $1,299 on. This is basically one of those TVs where, if you don't agree with Google's terms, you simply aren't allowed to use it...not even offline! A Disgusting practice.

Now when we look at the Smart features it's pretty cool, you can say things like Google turn on TV, and Google turn off TV, and almost like magic the TV turns on and off. This is really cool. Like James Bond tech cool. That being said, the picture quality has a ways to go. Now to be fair, you can get pretty Inky black levels, when there is high contrast did elements on the screen, or when you dim the backlight DRAMATICALLY. That being said the TV has a problem with glitching out. Every time I try to watch YouTube using the internal application, it would zoom in to nearly 100% of the screen, cropping out the entirety of the picture. This makes watching TV virtually impossible.

Now if you don't watch YouTube this isn't a big deal, but if you're like me and you're always on it, this is a deal-breaker. What's even worse, is that you've lost picture modes that you had last year, in addition to losing the ability to customize your cinemotion. This basically means you have less ability to control important aspects of picture quality and motion, leading to a really inconsistent experience. The x900f had all of these features, and is cheaper. So make no mistake you are getting scaled back on big-time. Sony may dress it up in a nice metallic build, wrapped in some nice smart features, but overall this television is a downgrade to increase sony oled sales. The X1 ultimate chip is almost a tease for sony, because the black levels are so bad, you'll wanna upgrade as soon as something with better black levels in the same price point comes out.

I find that when using this television, I couldn't help but notice if only the black levels were better this might actually be a television that could be worth my time. Simply put if you're somebody that likes to watch TV in a dark room, at reasonable levels of screen brightness, you're not going to enjoy this thing; If you're somebody that watches TV in a bright living room you're going to have solutely love this thing. That being said the colors are not quite as vibrant as qled from Samsung or Vizio at the moment, so those are better for color. Simply put if you have this kind of money to throw away, on a mediocre tv be my guest, as for Me I'll be looking for another product.

This tv comes so close, but yet so far away from what I'm looking for. And the worst part of all, is that it's completely on purpose to push bravia oled. Funny how my 2017 full array looks nothing like this, but magically all the tvs after Sony launched the a1e, their full array line has been getting worse and worse. I'm speaking with my wallet and I'm not going to be keeping this one. In summary, Too many glitches, forcing consumers to comply with Google even offline, downgraded features, lack of high frame-rate support, and a myriad of other problems makes the X950G a barely passable TV. For me though it's completely unpassable, and I would not be buying this one. Best of luck to all of those who end up with this TV.

Reason #2 is because you don't actively need to have the app open and in the background apps on Android, you can close it and it stays active as a persistent notification, whereas with Trackr I found it only does anything if I have the app open and in the background, which wastes more battery power than necessary, and isn't even aware of a Trackr that's lost battery power. That's not a good thing, as forgetting about replacing the coin cell batteries is easy to do. So this product took care of my two biggest concerns beautifully. Here's to hoping that I never need it, but now I feel a bit more secure.

title: Great in concept, horrible failure in reality!
text:
I loathe this device with the heat of a thousand suns! It seems like a spectacular device, and much lighter than a laptop when you need to backup photos when on the go. HOWEVER....
I brought this for a backpacking trip so I could use my iPhone XR as my only camera on the trail. I of course tried it out before the trip and found it intuitive and pretty easy to use through the app for pulling off photos and videos and then deleting the whole block. It was a little slow to transfer, but worked well enough. When I deleted my test block of media, it claimed it would clear up approx 16 GB of space but my phone only read it cleared about half of that amount (despite all the photos being off my phone). Everything transferred to my computer easily, although they were all named “copy” or some such.
Once I tried to use it on the trail a couple days later, however, I got all kinds of errors. First it said the drive was full (which it wasn’t). Then it would ask to boot the app when connected, but it wouldn’t read in the app as being connected and kept prompting me to plug in the device. Twice it opened the app and read as the drive being connected, but prompted me to make a folder as if it were an unformatted drive. A couple times it actually connected AND recognized the device AND started to transfer files, but after a few pictures it would quit and go back to the screen prompting me to connect the drive.
I followed all the troubleshooting tips multiple times to no avail.
I lost at least 2 hours of hiking due to fiddling with this thing, and another hour or two was spent hiking and still trying to make it work. I’m out the money because by the time I got home it was too late to return it. And worst, I missed the most awesome section of the Ice Age National scenic trail in almost 400 miles because I couldn’t take any more photos or video.
This is a great concept, but I would never count on one of these for anything important. And I’m beyond unhappy with the product in general. I can not recommend this in any way, shape, or form!

title: Five stars for me, maybe three or four for you?
text:
This is my my first mirrorless camera after years of using Canon SLR cameras and I must say that I am very pleased. The first thing I noticed was the slightly smaller size, likely due to it being a mirrorless camera. As someone with relatively small hands, this isn't a problem for me, although it may be for anyone with larger hands. The grip is very comfortable and the texture of the covering for the body is nice. I do like the AF/MF button on the back of the camera in a every easily accessible place without the need to search on the menu somewhere to switch from auto to manual focus.

I had never had a camera with a touch screen before and I had to remind myself at first to use it, rather than trying to move between screens and controls using wheels and buttons. The screen itself is a generous size and folds only vertically and not out to the side as was the case on my previous cameras. It can be raised vertically above the camera body to be visualized from the front of the camera if you are engaging in some self-portrait work or vide blogging, however it is difficult to tap on any controls that are on the bottom portion of the touch screen. Video bloggers who normally attach a mic to the camera may have a problem with the touchscreen being situated on the top of the camera since this can interfere with the attachment of a mic, whereas this is not a problem with a screen that is visible on the side of a camera. This is one of the reasons that some might give this camera only a four star rating. Not being a video blogger, this isn't an issue for me personally.

My kit included the electronic viewfinder. Frankly I have been accustomed to only taking pictures using a screen for so long that using a viewfinder seems somewhat strange to me but I'm glad that I now have this option. Time will tell whether I end up using it very much or not.

My kit featured the Canon 15-45mm lens. I know that a lot of people have complained about the small number of lenses available for this camera type. Although this lens is probably fine for all-round use, I have ordered the 18-150mm f/3.5-6.3 IS STM and the 11-22mm f/4-5.6 IS STM, which seem to be the most popular other lens for this camera besides the 22mm f/2 STM wide angle. Keep in mind that you can purchase an adapter that will allow you to use Canon's EF lenses, if you already have them in your bag.

I really haven't had this camera long enough to provide any comments about the quality of the pictures or videos that the camera produces, which, of course, is the most important thing when considering the purchase of a camera and I may update this review at a later time if I experience anything that makes me back off of my current five star rating but so far I have no complaints with this camera, which is well-suited for my own needs. Your own needs may be different than mine and thus your rating may vary.

title: The Pi Is in the Fridge!
text:
Can't believe I bought a cooler with RGB lights but here it is. Like all on my computers, if I am now actually sitting in front of it, then it's running some distributed-processing app like the old seti. I use 100% of available processors 85% of the time. The color is supposed to indicate temperature and its all blue and green. Just checked a temperature sensor in the Pi and its reading 47 C. Sounds pretty good to me.

The mounting is interesting. There is a translucent plastic plate that is held below the motherboard by standoff screws which attach to standoff plugs on the top of the motherboard. Two oddly shaped pieces of metal attach to the bottom of the tower and can be arranged in several ways. For example, I have one tower attached in what I assume is the "default" position that leaves the GPIO pins wide open and another turned the opposition direction so that the ribbon cable for a camera can run forwards or backwards while still leaving the GPIO pins accessible. These metal pieces have holes on their ends that fit over the threaded top of standoffs and are held down using small nuts.

The tower comes with one extra standoff, screw for bottom plate, and nut for the top standoff. It also includes three small "thermal pads." I wasn't thrilled and didn't want to stack them to get good contact but then I had to remove a tower from one Pi that had to be returned and saw that it did have indentations from being squeezed between the CPU and base of the tower. BTW, the bottom is not a miracle of machining tolerances. The heat pipes were not completely flush with the metal block that formed the base but I could see impressions in the pad for not only the heat tubes but the outline of the block. As I said - 41 C at 85% full load for 24/7 so I'd say it was doing its job (this is for the one that was removed and reinstalled with a fresh thermal pad).

title: Unreliable and Corrupts Data
text:
Got these for Christmas 2019. Didn't take them out of the packaging for a while because I didn't have a need for them. In May 2020, I pulled the 1st cable out of it's packaging to take a disk image of my fileserver's hard drive in my USB 3 dock, since my fileserver didn't have a USB 3.0 controller in it.

I then tried to take the disk image. The 1st attempt immediately failed with a bogus "out of space" error. I tried again, and it failed several hours in with an error that I don't remember. I think it was something about not being able to transfer or read data from the source drive (fileserver HDD). I tried it again, only for it to fail in a very spectacular manner. I came back to the computer after letting it run all night, and there was garbage all over the screen, things were flashing, the screen itself was garbled, and there was a number that kept going up very fast.

So I shut it down, took the 2nd cable out of it's packaging, and tried the whole operation again. Every single imaging attempt using either of these cables failed in some way or another, caused by data corruption happening on the cable itself as the data passed through it. I wrote off both cables as trash, abandoned the imaging attempt, and reverted everything back to normal.

Now here's the worst part: These cables corrupt data that passes through them. When I checked the SMART stats on my fileserver's HDD before I attempted the imaging attempts, it reported zero (0) ECC errors. After I had attempted the imaging attempts, it reported more than 240. All of those errors were caused by the drive receiving corrupted data, attempting to correct it, and failing.
When I put the HDD back into the fileserver and booted it back up, fsck (File System ChecK, I run Linux on my systems) ran and found filesystem corruption, which it then fixed. It also had corrupted logs, which were discarded.

DO NOT purchase these cables unless you want nothing but frustration and corrupted data.

title: Some features changed from previous cases
text:
I generally love the Fintie products... cases and apple pencil holder, and have bought many Fintie brand products.
I am disappointed with my Fintie Case with Built-in Pencil Holder for iPad Pro 11" 2020 & 2018 [Support 2nd Gen Pencil Charging

CONS:
1. There are only 2 slots for the iPad to sit in; previous models had 3 slots
2. The fabric of the interior is more slippery than previous cases
Therefore, I cannot prop my iPad vertical enough for reading, and for drawing I find that it slips out of the slots as soon as I put my Apple pencil down. I think, Fintie, that these features would be easy for you to modify in future cases that you make for my iPad pro 11" 2020, which I intend to own for the next 4-6 years. I would gladly purchase another case from you if you added a third slot for the iPad to sit in, and if the fabric were less slippery.
3. I think one of the corners that my iPad sits in is not a snug fit. I worry that this case is not good, if my iPad falls, it could land on the glass face. But I have not found another case I prefer. I really do love the 360˚ rotation feature.

3. There was another feature I loved with my first Fintie case for my iPad Pro 9.7", which was a 3" wide elastic band that I could slip my hand it, when I was reading on the iPad, so I could easily hold the iPad. I was really sorry to see this feature go.

PROS:
1. well, I love the 360˚ turning feature of this Fintie case, and the fact that there is a cover. I could not find another iPad Pro 11" 2020 case that has both 360˚ rotation AND a cover for the case. So this feature was what made my buying decision for this Fintie case.
2. I love that the pencil has a slot where it is safe and always charging.
3. The color and pattern choices are nice.
4. It does have auto sleep

I have to say, every time my iPad slips out of the slot when I am drawing, and every time I want my iPad propped up a little more vertically, I come back to Amazon to search for a new brand or model of case that might replace this Fintie that I have.

So there you have it... only a 3 Star, Fintie...
I wrote you an email about this a month ago, but never heard back from you... therefore, I am posting this average review...

title: Incredible Value for a fancy product...
text:
[[VIDEOID:ff6de842efc5c0a4331dd1f636ec0ac2]] To those of you who are in the market for a new computer case, let me share with you this wonderful case by Montech.

Its the Montech Air 900 ARGB-Black. Now a little background, since 2016, Telon Co. (a Taiwanese PC manufacturer for 30 years) has been trying to get into the US Market. Well, they succeeded and I have to tell you that this case is incredible for the price and features.

Features Include - But not limited to:

Addressable RGB (for the Gamer wanting to make a statement)

Expansion Slots x 8

I/O Ports:
USB2.0 x 2
USB3.0 x 2
Audio x 1
Mic x 1
LED Manual control button

Fan Support:
Front -120mm x 3/140mm x 2
Rear - 120mm x 1
Top - 120/140mm x 2
(Does include a front and rear fan w/o LED features)

Can support Radiator:
Front - 120/140/240/280/360mm
Rear - 120mm
Top - 120/140/240/280mm

Clearance for the gamer and Content maker:
VGA 370mm
CPU 165mm

Dust Filters for:
Top, bottom & one in the front on mine

Power Supply Support:
Bottom mount, ATX

Lighting Support:
Front RGB LED Strip x 2 (which you see a little of the feature in the video)

Now lets talk Drive support:

Well, this case can contain up to 5 x 2.5" SSD and 2 x 3.5"HDD.

If you think the features are nice now, this unit has a variety of motherboard sizes to support such as:
E-ATX
ATX
Micro ATX and Mini ITX

Now, speaking from a PC hobbyist's perspective...while migrating my gear from a ThermalTake Armor case (Full Tower) to this more condensed size, it was not without some challenges but it worked out. I love how this company not only used a reasonably good light-weight material for the case, I also love how they added a cavity under the motherboard area that was used to cable manage my computer. To tell you the truth, I don't recall have as a good a look inside a case as I do now. I am using a ATX motherboard and a AMD Ryzen 2700x Processesor. I am also using a MSI Nvidia RTX 2060 card too.

Because the cable management was well done, I can sit back and enjoy the RGB activity knowing that I have a pretty clean setup. The only trouble I can speak on is that...while installing my spacer screws, it was difficult to get them screwed in without a little bit of force. A word of caution to would-be hobbyists, do not go hog wild on screwing the spacer screws in because doing so could cause you to strip the hold and considering the vibration that your processor fan could be exerting can make keeping your motherboard tight.

Regardless, this product has an affordable price tag, looks sleek and clean and it has a ton of features, you are sure to get a solid case. Just be patient with yourself when you are cable managing and trying to wire your RGB rigs. That can be challenging in itself. Happy building.

text:

About a week later the cloudiness did clear up, but have left that very same cloudy residue on my reservoir and CPU/GPU blocks are now caked with some kind of residue trapped within the fins on the cold plate. The blocks and reservoir will now need to be disassembled and cleaned when comes the time for loop maintenance. Which just increases the chances of a leak occurring as the seal is now broken.

It only gets 1 start because its coolant and works as intended in terms of cooling. Overall, disappointing.

title: Really good solution for PoE on Lightning devices
text: My company deploys iPhones and IPads in commercial environments and we needed a PoE solution.  We ended up testing both the PoE Texas devices and the Belkin solution.  These PoE Texas devices worked great.  Plug and play out of the box, even with older devices like iPhone 6s phones.  They are compact and support GigE.  The Belkin adapters did allow for a lightning-based power source (making it both a regular Ethernet adapter + Power port and PoE), but otherwise, it is at least twice as large as these adapters and only got half the speed (around 300-400 Mbps).  I've already deployed over 20 of these adapters and they have really saved the day for us.  My only complaint is the rather large 90 degree lightning connector, which impact some cases we used.

title: Great Sound - One Note of Caution
text:
My collection is mostly classical but I also like, ... well, Roy Orbison plus some 60s rock. My late husband used to say that I have multiple personality disorder.

These speakers sound fabulous with a wide range of sound. The high end is flawless. I have these paired with a mid-price subwoofer. Overall, the low end is excellent. I recalibrated (Onkyo) but I might experiment with the crossover setting.

These replaced some relatively inexpensive JBL speakers. The difference was noticeable with the first note of music.

That "note of caution:" My speaker stands are small platform. They hold the speaker "securely" with adjustable pressure pads on both sides. The problem is that the speakers have a rounded edge preventing the pads from really gripping. If I tighten them, the speaker rises up like it was squeezed from a toothpaste tube and I end up gripping air.

I ordered some heavy duty Velcro fasteners which should do the trick.

These speakers have a proprietary securing mechanism on the bottom but the Q Acoustic stands are ridiculously priced (IMO).

Bottom line: Terrific sound from reasonably priced speakers. Excellent value. Just evaluate your mounting options in advance.

title: Great device, can't get enough to meet my compute needs.

title: Budget 27" Monitor - Would be great if not for quality control issues
text:
This monitor is hard to love due to some glaring issues with its quality control. That being said, it's a budget conscious monitor that has a MSRP of $129.99 so you have to be realistic with your expectations. I'll go through my experience for you from start to finish.

The Pros - It is 75hz refresh rate capable. 5ms response time for those who need it. It's light weight and very thin. (Great for mounting) It has 2 HDMI connectors. The version that I got uses a 12V DC port (Useful for cable management). Built in speakers a plus if you have limited space to work with. (Like using the monitor at a work station / terminal)

The Cons - Out of 2 ordered, 1 had a dead pixel. The speakers are not only muffled, but extremely quiet. Stand is extremely light weight for a 27 inch monitor. 12V 3A AC/DC adapter looks really suspect (like the ones you get with LED strips) and probably will fail over time. VESA specs are incorrect in the manual. (They recommend M4 12mm screws). 1 year only warranty that requires you to send it back to them on your dime for service.

My biggest gripe so far (dead pixel or not) is that the VESA mounting holes on the rear of the monitor are extremely shallow. I needed to special order a set of M4 8mm screws in order to get it to attach to one of my dual monitor brackets. VESA standards list 100 x 100 hole patterns to use a standard M4 10mm screw. My 8mm screws that I ordered barely fit into my bracket with a washer. I would assume the holes drilled in the monitor for the screws are 4mm or 5mm deep at best. The manual recommends using 12mm M4 screws! That would leave about 8mm or 7mm jutting out in the air. Most VESA mounting hardware will only include 10mm, 12mm and 25mm M4 screws for 100 x 100 hole patterns. So in case you want to mount this monitor to any bracket, make sure to have some shorter M4 screw sizes ready.

Negatives aside, it's an extremely attractive monitor for the home office or the kids (teenager or college bound). You can forgive a lot of the imperfections if this is going to be attached to something you don't stare at constantly. Probably also good for grass roots e-sports tournament organizers who need a larger screen real estate but don't want to break the bank and aren't too worried about ultra quality. 5ms response time and 75hz refresh rate is good for most games except ultra competitive FPS.

This is going to be a dynamic review in that I will update my experience as I own the monitor longer. I have a replacement coming from Amazon for the dead pixel afflicted one I got initially and we'll see how that goes. Sceptre's policy on dead pixels is that they need "5 or more" to be considered defective enough for warranty service. Worst yet, you have to ship the item back to them at your expense. So I highly recommend while you're in the Amazon 30 day return window to put the monitor through its paces and see if it's the right one for you without any major problems. Once it's out of that window, you'll be at the mercy of Sceptre's RMA department and will probably need to pay $22 bucks (or more) to send it back to fix a $129.99 (or less) monitor.

text:
Using the most recent Beta drivers (7/7). A couple glitches that I’ve encountered:
* The overlay that shows temp/speed/voltage goes away after a few minutes in a game (leaving a pixelated splotch where it used to be)
* Streaming a steam game (AC Origins) to an Oculus Quest via Virtual Desktop (which worked with a 480) stops after a minute in game and Virtual Desktop’s error suggests updating video drivers.

Pros:
* Very good FPS/$.
* Streams Amazon Prime video to a Quest via Virtual Desktop like a champ (built in support for the HEVC compression).
* “Auto-undervolt” in WattMan lowers temps by 4-6 degrees while increasing performance (in TimeSpy benchmark).

* Drivers need a few updates (see above)
* No sign of getting the 3 months of Xbox Game Pass that some people are getting when buying 5700 XTs from other retailers.
* Without undervolting, temperatures at load get up to 83 degrees Celsius (for reference, CPU in the same case isn’t going over 57).

Probably wisest to wait for versions of this card that come with 3rd party coolers (sometime in August) - especially if you don’t use over-ear headphones.

title: Made Cutting the Cord Easier
text:
I was wasting money on cable channels since we only watched network TV and streamed online. I bought this mostly because I wanted DVR functionality without recurring fees. I don't use it so much for actually watching live TV as I do strictly for the ability to record and watch broadcast things I can't stream. Using my old attic antenna, it's able to pick up roughly 50-60 channels in the northern Washington, DC suburbs.

The channel guide takes longer than I'd like to populate. For free you can see the channel guide for 24 hours into the future. If you want to pay a monthly, annual, or lifetime fee, you can get more. The more difficult hurdle I see is that if you don't have the paid guide, you can only schedule DVR recordings by channel and time slot instead of by show. So, if a show airs at a different time, you need to manually reschedule it. With the paid guide, all shows record under one entry in the DVR menu and you select episodes from there. If you don't have the paid guide, it records each instance under a separate menu entry with a single episode in there without any easy way to tell which episode is which. (Problematic if you're recording old shows where the air date means nothing.) It's very cumbersome. If you're prepared to spend money for their guide (when an OTA guide is broadcast for free) just so you have more convenient recording, then factor that into your mental price for this unit. I've seen that the 4-tuner model includes the guide for a year (?) instead of the short free trial the 2-tuner model gives. Something to keep in mind.

I use this with a Roku, but I have installed the app on my LG smart TVs as well.

Overall I'm happy with it. The interface could be slightly better, but maybe a software update will improve that eventually.

title: It's alright
text:
Pros: Screen, Graphics Card, Speaker quality, boot speed
Cons: Gets warm, Screenpad, Keyboard

Been using this for about 3 months at the time of this review and have to admit I'm a little disappointed. After paying $1300 for a laptop, this came with more issues than I would've liked. One of the major problems I have had is that if I don't turn off the laptop completely before I go to sleep, it will wake from sleep every night around 12 AM due to a certain Windows 10 function that conducts automatic update checks. I'm very tech savvy but after searching through multiple forums and trying many solutions, there's no way to permanently disable or reschedule it. This may not be a huge problem for many but in some cases where I don't want to have to reopen all of the programs I'm using the next day or forget to turn it off, this issue is something to think of if you can relate. I haven't seen anyone else mention this in their review so I may have just been unlucky in my unit but just keep this in mind. One of the first nights I had it, it did this and I woke up to find it on after ~8 hours and it was extremely hot. This is to be expected from them packing an i7 processor in such a thin metal body. I would recommend purchasing a cheap laptop cooler for this problem as the fans seem to kick on without it being under much load.

Display/Graphics card:
The 4k screen is beautiful and sharp but I do most of my work on an external 1080p monitor, keep in mind that you can run into some scaling issues with certain programs, in my case, iTunes is a little blurry on the laptop screen but if changing the scaling settings to optimize it for 4k, all of the icons become extremely small and it is a difficult to read without straining my eyes. In regards to image quality, one issue I had that I just recently solved was that some programs had some extreme sharpening issues. At first I thought this had to do with the 4k to 1080p scaling on my external monitor but then I realized it had to do with the NVIDIA graphics card. Luckily there is a built in app where you can customize the graphic card settings and I was able to disable image sharpening, resolving the issue.

Performance:
I'm not a huge gamer but it renders blender scenes at a very decent speed. I also do a lot of multimedia work using Photoshop, After Effects, and Premiere, and this laptop preforms well. It also has no problem running multiple tabs of chrome and other programs all at once. Note that the fans do run often and ASUS does not allow you to manually control speed. So if you plan on using this in a quiet, public environment, be aware that it does not run silent for long.

Thermals:
Like I mentioned earlier however, packing an i7 processor into such a thin metal frame isn't the best combination. The top part of the keyboard extremely hot when the computer is under load for extended periods of time. If I weren't using a bluetooth keyboard, I would imagine the laptop being quite uncomfortable to use due to the heat. The lower parts of the frame like the palm rest area feel fine but you can feel the heat radiating off of the top portion if you just hover your hand over it, and the metal could definitely cause burns if you touch it for more than a few seconds. I'm not sure laptop coolers have any notable effect on helping temperatures but I would recommend buying one anyway for peace of mind and since they're relatively cheap (got one off Amazon for ~$30). You also aren't able to undervolt this processor to help thermal performance, something I didn't know until after I purchased it and attempted to do so myself.

Keyboard:
I actually use a separate keyboard and mouse so I haven't typed extensively on the built in keyboard. The keys feel a bit mushy in my opinion but at least it isn't loud to type on. The keyboard backlight offers 3 levels but only the highest brightness level is usable and only at night. In any environment with light, the backlight is almost impossible to see. It also isn't evenly lit across all keys and even individual keycaps may have sections that are not uniform in lighting.

Screenpad:
I had no intention of using the Screenpad when I first ordered it and wished that there was a cheaper version without it. After having the laptop for 3+ months I still feel the same way. It may seem cool in concept to some but in reality it is not practical. Even using it as an extra display isn't pleasant due to the viewing angle and how tiny everything appears. I almost always have it turned off, and can count on one hand the number of times I've actually tried to use it.

Battery:
I always have it plugged in and haven't gotten a chance to test the battery life since I'm not at university due to pretty obvious circumstances lol. But I like that the myAsus software allows you to configure settings such as only allowing up to a 60% charge to prolong the overall life of the battery.

Misc:
-When I'm not using headphones, I find the laptop's built in speakers to be great. Even at medium volume, audio is loud and clear.
-Windows Hello is great and works seemingly instantly and it boots up very fast even from being completely off, which is to be expected from a device packing these specs.
-Wish there were a few more ports. Paying this much for a laptop and it only has one USB-C and 2 USB-A is a bit underwhelming but this is an issue many premium ultrabooks suffer from as well. At least there's a full size SD card reader for those who do a lot of photography/video editing.

title: Don’t pass this webcam by. Easy to Use, plug and go.
text:
[[VIDEOID:65cb9c0451587cc2fd618277df96386a]] I was looking for a webcam and have always relied upon Logitech products. Of course, those are back ordered and the ones available, the prices have been increased dramatically - not nice!

The E Costal 1080p was priced low, how low? Well, I was going to pass on by this one because I did not think it would be any good. Desperate, I thought I’d give it a try.

I have an older Mac laptop - Mid 2012. It still has a couple of years left in her, but the video quality is lacking. I needed to upgrade to 1080p for better quality vlogs, video, video podcasts which we use Zoom to do.

The webcam was easy to install, the best part, no apps, driver, hardware to fiddle with. Seriously, just clip to the back of your laptop, plug and it’s ready. My laptop instantly recognized it.

The quality is quite good and an improvement over my laptop’s camera. There is a bit of a fish-eye effect on the edges, but not too much to stop you from trying this out.

There is no zoom or autofocus which, I prefer; less monkeying around with. Once you clip it on your laptop you can easily move the camera side-to-side, up-and-down without it falling off the laptop. It’s quite sturdy.

This webcam is also tripod ready. I love this part. I record cooking DIY’s and other types of videos and love the flexibility to have it off the laptop to record where I want and yet, still use the laptop as a monitor. Brilliant.

Seriously, if you are looking for a webcam, and don’t want to pay inflated- demand prices for other webcams, give this one a try. It is perfect for conferences, Zoom, YouTube, vlogs, videos and live streams. I am super happy with this webcam.

title: Beautiful slim case/cover that fits great
text:
Just got the phone case today. It fits my Moto G7 perfectly! I'm not sure why there's so many reviews saying it doesn't fit? Just be sure you pick the correct model and you should be fine.

I love that this is a slim cover and doesn't add a bunch of bulk to my phone. The back is a firm slightly flexible material that feels like a hard plastic or something similar at least. The holes line up great and the buttons are precise. I can click power, volume up and volume down no problem. Both cameras appear to be unobstructed from what I can tell so far as well.

The design is gorgeous as well, which is the main reason I went with this case. I got the teal/pink marble with holographic highlights. It's a little hard to tell from the picture, but basically all of the wide "cracks" in the marble design is one big sheet of holographic material. The linear holographic reflection is uniform across a large area of the phone as you turn it against the light and it's beautiful.

I went ahead and applied the screen protector as well since it came with one, and that went on smoothly without any issue. I recommend putting the back on first, and getting a feel for where you will apply it by placing the screen protector over the screen before peeling the plastic off the adhesive. I was able to use the lip from the case to help line up the screen protector how it should go, and it had a little give to slide it over a hair since I didn't quite line it up 100% correctly at first.

It feels like solid/durable material to me, so I'm giving that 5 stars for now. If it turns out to be less durable after I've had it longer I can always come back and edit the review. I'll try to remember to come back and edit it further down the line anyway in case I come across some issue with it or just to testify that it's still going strong. I'm very happy with this case for the price!

At $149 (Later was solicited for same camera at $129), if working properly, this may be useable as a v-blogging camera.. I wouldn't know. It didn't work properly, and I do not V-Blog.

If you are videoing something that you must capture... and that may create a lifetime memory, I believe either a functioning lower resolution camera or saving to spend more money o a better camera would be the best way to go.

I have a standard resolution Canon, and a JVC that still work, are smooth to operate and very reliable. Just purchased a HD Canon for another $100 ... it will be in tomorrow and I will fully test it before I miss another Track meet.
To recap:
Simple , reduced list of functions This would be ok, but they are not easy to use, nor are they intuitive.
Awkward ergonomics
Lighting not consistent
Video pixelates, freezes and drops out, as if it was receiving a bad broadcast.

I cannot recommend purchasing this camera unless it is your only option.

Good luck.

Thanks to Amazon for making return so smooth. it was salve on a potentially bad wound!

title: Mediocre performance, Router Syslog was riddled with errors
text:
I have installed a number of TP-Link Deco devices for my parents and in-laws. They have great coverage and are pretty darn fast. I bought this router for our small home thinking we'd get faster speeds and than from the Deco M5 system since we have a 500mbps connection. The router booted up the first time and things were okay. The coverage was mediocre and the speeds didn't seem to be much faster than the Decos I was comparing it to. The decos provided 150mbps in most places but I couldn't get anywhere close to the 440mbps I was getting right next to the router.

When I tried to update the firmware and all hell broke loose. The router couldn't find the server, nor could it find the time server to automatically update the date and time. I downloaded the correct firmware and updated it myself but the router kept rebooting. I looked at the system log and it was riddled with errors. I reset everything to factory settings and tired again with no luck. (I am 100% sure I updated this with the right firmware). The error that kept arising was "config import failed"

If you're thinking a tri-band expensive router is going to blow you away look somewhere else. While this system is supposed to be faster than the Deco M5s I found it only to be 10-20% faster on the 5Hz channels. Combine this with the fact that straight out of the box it wouldn't update itself nor could it even set the time I'm sending this back and getting a set of M9 Plus's.

I had high hopes for this system and while maybe I just got a lemon I'm moving on. Proceed with caution.

title: Be very careful!
text:
I purchased three of these and send two of them two my sisters who each live over 300 miles away from our mother. The intention was to record mother's day messages for our mom. Well, two of them are perfect. One of them slides very easily so when trying to listen to my sister's message, I accidentally recorded over it because I didn't realize it had moved while in my hand. The two my other sister and I got are much tighter and don't slide as easily. Since I know it'll take me months to go to the post office to send it back to her, I just ordered another one for her to record again.

So my recommendation is don't be a dolt, like me, and be 100% certain that it is on either O or P before you press the button. Once you are 100% certain you are happy with the message, use tape or something to hold the slider in place so it can't move once it is in the finished object.

As far as sound quality, my sister's recording sounds a bit distant but absolutely sounds like her. I held it about a foot away from my face while recording my message and it is very clear and good volume and (unfortunately) sounds just like me (anyone else hate the sound of their own voice).

I find the cost of these recorders to be just right and the shipping was free and very fast with Prime.

Once my sister sends me the new recording, these will get inserted into crocheted stuffed hearts for my mom and she will cry and life will be good!

I've run them over quite a few cycles now, thousands of shots, and they don't seem to be fading - still holding at or just a hair under what the oly batteries are doing. They seem to hold charge when not used about on par with Oly batt too. They charge quickly both with the included charger AND the Olympus charger that came with the camera, so, yes, they are fully chipped/coded (or decoded, however you want to call it). The oly battery charges on this charger fine too. Sometimes the % doesn't seem accurate with other off-brands - not so with these - they seem to smoothly count down from 100% to 0% and though I usually don't run them dead, I've tried it a couple times with these and they steadily approach then sit at 0% for a bit instead drifting to 10%, the immediately plummeting to 2% and then dying suddenly like my Dell notebook does! That predictability is very nice - you can plan your battery swap with confidence. BOTH batteries seem to drift to "dead" similarly; again, the consistency is nice.

I often prefer name-brand batteries (nikon for nikon gear, canon for canon, oly for oly, Sony for Sony, GoPro for GoPro, etc) but for the price I'm more than satisfied with these. Those few extra shots that I really can't tell if I get ... for the price, I just swap batteries and move on as they are sooooo close I'd be swapping in a couple minutes anyway and I like to swap before camera shuts down anyway, so no real impact on my shooting. In all other respects, I can't tell these from brand batteries.

title: Your Arduino IDE version changes what board/processor you need to select.
text:
As for the board: so far so good. Cheap, works as intended, an annoyance to setup as others have mentioned, and I'd rather have a micro USB, but overall I'm satisfied. One star off for the difficulty in setup (read on for how I got mine to work; it literally involved a random hunch), otherwise a good board for permanently embedding in a project as its small and inexpensive.

----- Instructions for use current as of 6/27/2020 -----

Just got one of my boards working. I was following the advice of other reviewers who mentioned you need to select Arduino Nano as your board and ATmega328P (Old Bootloader) as your processor. Turns out this might have worked in the past, or for particular people's setups, but it did not work for mine. Here's how I got things to function:

First off, I'm using the 1.8.13 version of the Arduino IDE, which is the most current as of this review (6/27/2020). I can't guarantee this is what caused the issue, but I'm going to assume its part of it. I'm running Windows 10 Home, 64 bit, version 10.0.17134 Build 17134. Your mileage may vary if you are running a different version or a different OS entirely.

When I initially plugged the nano into my computer, I could not see any COM port appear. I had already installed the CH340 drivers (you can do so from elegoo.com/download, or from Sparkfun at https://learn.sparkfun.com/tutorials/how-to-install-ch340-drivers/all). Turns out my first mistake was a simple one: I didn't use a data cable. The cable I found lying around turned out to be for power only. Keep this in mind. The way you can tell is if the Nano starts running the LED blink program, but is not discovered by your computer. The blink program will run as it comes preloaded so it will run when the board is powered on. This means either you have a power-only cable, or somehow the data pins have been damaged (less likely that only those pins specifically would be damaged, but who knows... its possible). Switching out the cable fixed the discovery issue.

I still couldn't upload to the board though. Once the board was discoverable, I then began following video instructions from the Sparkfun page I linked to above. They said to re-run the CH340 driver executable, uninstall the drivers, then reinstall them. This time I got a message saying the drivers had been installed correctly, rather than having been "pre-installed" as was mentioned before. I tried uploading again, but no luck. Still, the drivers do need to be installed correctly so this was probably a secondary issue. Who knows, but I'm going with that. I could now see a new populated COM port, so I knew the Nano was being seen now.

I once again set my IDE settings to Arduino Nano as the board, ATmega328P (Old Bootloader) as the processor, and finally the new COM port as the port. Still nothing. As a last ditch effort, I tried switching the board to Arduino Uno.

"Done uploading."

What do you know... it worked. Why? Who knows... but it did. I hope this helps somebody else out with this odd situation.

title: Charges batteries more fully than basic chargers
text:
When this EBL charger arrived I put in a battery that was "fully" charged with an AmazonBasics charger. Sure enough, the charger indicated that it required further charging. Other reviews complain about how long it takes to charge batteries, but that happens when you're charging your batteries past 80%. The "fast charge" portion is as fast as the AmazonBasics charger, but the final trickle charge takes its time so as not to damage your cells. I'm not seeing any overnight charge times, but I don't run my batteries completely dead.

This unit charges batteries individually! Many chargers at this price require you to charge in pairs, and turn off when the most fully charged battery is done. When a cell is done charging in this unit, the current to the battery stops. You can tell because the battery that finishes first is cooler to the touch than the others.

The batteries do get quite warm in the charger. Not warm enough to burn your hand, but warm enough that you can't use them right away. Ten minutes and they're at room temperature in a 70F room.

The charger has a three segment indicator. From what I can figure, if the battery shows empty with one bar flashing, it's at 25% or less. One bar solid and one flashing, 50%. Two bars solid and one flashing, 75% or above and doing the final trickle charge.

Pros:
- Individual battery charging.
- Doesn't shut off the whole unit when the first battery is done
- Individual charge level display
- Long trickle charge to charge batteries fully
- Inexpensive

Cons:
- Batteries hard to remove. You have to turn it upside down and whack it against your palm to pop the batteries out.
- Batteries get very warm, which means longer cool down time before you can use them.

Other:
Power plug is offset to the left, which may be a blessing or a curse. If you're plugging into the last outlet on a power strip, it keeps the body of the charger out of the way. If you've got switch or any other plugs to the right, you wont be able to plug it in.

title: Impressive
text: I've been looking for a decent portable monitor for my 11 inch MacBook Air because (1) the built-in display is a bit small and (2) I really like working with two monitors.  I'd seen some of the bigger, better-known brands but they were too expensive and worse, according to the reviews, didn't seem to play well with a lot of computers.  I saw the Lepow and all the positive displays.  When I saw a deal on one, I went ahead and ordered it.  I've had the monitor now for three days and I'm pretty happy with the purchase.  The monitor was well packaged, arrived quickly and set-up took five minutes or less.  My Air lacks a USB C but the standard USB provided ample power and the hdmi worked just fine.  Resolution, brightness, and picture quality were fine for my uses which include basics like word processing to web surfing to Photoshop and page layout with inDesign.  The larger, second screen makes this a small screen Air a machine I can actually get work done on.  As others have pointed out, the sound is pretty lame but it's no problem to us the Air speakers or better still, a decent usb speaker.  All in all, I'm very happy with my purchase and if you're looking for a portable monitor that gets the job one without breaking the bank and just works I'd seriously reccomend this one.

title: sounds solid and punchy,easy to install..great value for the money
text: hello...i have a jeep jk sport...basic as could be... I really enjoy music and as time went on I wished I bought an "upgraded" jeep with premium sound. Well I up graded all 4 speakers 2 in sound bar and 2 in lower dash..that made a difference but not "bumping" as I would like... I would crank up a song I loved and it sound good...but loud-if that makes sense-..so I searched amazon for a while and decided to buy this amplified subwoofer, mainly because I saw others who owned Jeeps bought this and was happy. So I purchased this subwoofer and a separate amp install kit that had long power wire,weatherproof fuse,eyelets,zip ties ect....found that here on amazon...so this amp arrived, and what do you know?! Q20 happened...now I have plenty of time to install this amp...using the wires from the install kit i ordered separate,...I searched for a perfect spot to install this amp////thinking i could mount under the front seats..... it didn't fit...I could have mounted it to the rear door as seen in pics on this product description, but i already have rear view camera wires there...I could have mounted anywhere in the jeep with the provided mounts, but I did not want to drill or screw holes in my jeep...so I found simply laying it behind drivers seat (i have 2 door jeep) was perfect...yep just kind of sits there on an angle and doesn't slide around...I ran power wire and "switched" hot wire to the amp, I used "high input" supplied wires due to the ease of accessing the left/tight speaker outputs from the right roll bar under foam protecting,,,I found wire colors on google...very easy.... I found a great ground on the side if the center console....inch's away from the amp...I removed both securing bolts, slid ground up behind console so the eyelet was directly on console mounting bracket and lowered console back down and re-secured factory bolt.....no holes drilled!!! then the control switch was super easy...I ran that up under roll bar cover down the side, out by drivers sun visor and mounted control switch above rear view mirror....I did secure that into the plastic molding....no holes drilled into the vehicle body!...once installed and a few moments of tweaking....I test drove the jeep with the amp on and was very impressed!  I am very happy with the "remote" to control bass output...and location I placed it... now songs sound loud without being "loud" and the bass music can be felt! vibrates the jeeps floor boards! I listen to Sirius Lithium, Ozzy's Boneyard, Pop Rock's, Hit's One, Rush, Stone Temple Pilots, SoundGarden,  ect...just to give you an idea of types of music....the bass addition makes music sounds full complete loud warm and rich! If you are looking for as I just described, this is a great choice..... if you want to be the guy that goes thump thump with lousy distortion and want to be heard blocks away, this is too good for you... this is an affordable quality good looking full rich sounding bass that can be adjusted per song as needed with the supplied wired remote switch....easy to install....took me 3 hours because I wanted it perfect looking- I tie strapped and cloth taped all wires to give a minimal intrusive look...If i had to do it in a rush it could have taken me an hour....and the best part...besides looking good and sounding good....there is no engine noise or whining through this bass system.. very nice...

title: Go with a higher quality switch
text:
So I bought this because it was a good deal for what I thought was a decent unmanaged switch at the time. I use a mesh system but I wanted a few hardwired spots for specific pieces of hardware. I didn't necessarily need a 16 port but as I said it was a good deal at the time.

Switch worked good for a couple of months with no issues. It's set up in my cool dry basement be in a newer home so heat and humidity are not a problem. It was also set up in an open an accessable area in case I ever wanted to move plugs around. About 2 weeks ago while out on a business trip all of my home systems suddenly went down abruptly. I thought it was the router or modem so I had a friend come to the house and reset everything. Worked fine for a few hours before everything went down again. This time for 2 days. I could ping the modem so I know the ISP was not the issue. Came home and reset every again and it worked for a few hours and then went down once again. Tried trouble shooting once piece at a time and low and behold everything worked great with no issues on the mesh for days with no loss of connection once I took the switch out. I thought what the heck, this could be a fluke so I plugged the switch back in just to give it a test. Everything worked fine for about 24 hours and then the same thing happened once again.

Went to check back here on Amazon and saw several recent reviews of this switch with people having similar issues with this switch prematurely failing from one thing or the other.

The switch seems like it's an overheating issue but again I have it about as open an area that it can be with nothing blocking airflow but considering this has no fan there is no way for me to quantify this so in any case I believe this sale back of switches is on sale for a reason and it's because they are trash.

Also in reading the recent reviews I see that there have been several issues with netgear customer service so I am not even going to bother trying with this garbage and will be replacing it with higher quality switch from a different manufacturer.

TLDR: This thing is garbage and don't waste your money. Go with a higher quality switch from a different manufacturer.
