title: Works with USB 2.0 at 1920x1080
text: The most difficult part about researching these USB/HDMI converters is finding one that works with USB 2.0 and at what resolution. Most of these cover USB 3.x, which is fine but I have USB 2.0. Several talk about being compatible with USB 2.0 but then don't mention the resolution. A couple mention USB 2.0 but their max resolution is 800x600! I'm using this USB/HDMI adapter with a Samsung 32" curved monitor at 1920x1080 on USB 2.0. My only issue is and this is most likely more a monitor issue is that sometimes the secondary monitor on the USB/HDMI adapter doesn't turn on. I have the USB/HDMI adapter plugged into a USB hub so that might be the problem. If I were to go directly to the computer, this may not be an issue. However I need to run it through the USB hub because I'm sharing the monitor (and other USB devices) with another computer. The resolution when this problem with the secondary monitor not starting up is pretty simple. On my USB hub, each USB port has an on/off switch. I just cycle the switch to off for 5 or so seconds for the USB/HDMI adapter and turn it back on. The monitor then recognizes the USB/HDMI adapter and turns on. I use the secondary monitor for mainly browsing the Internet, word processing and such. I'm not a gamer so I can't say how well it'll perform under such circumstances. title: Great Product, light weight, but sturdy, and very portable in its' case
text:
I was slightly apprehensive about this item, as I did not know how light weight it might be. The backdrop screen that I ordered is a vary large screen, and I was concerned about the stand tipping over. Well, let me tell you, the stand held my big backdrop with zero problems. The tubing is light weight, but strong enough to handle things. The clamps are outstanding and easily clamp onto my backdrop. The pieces of the stand are telescoping and easily adjustable, just like a normal camera tripod. Have to tell you, after looking around a bit, that this item, with its' included case, is a very good product. There are many others that sell the stand, but with no case. You have to look for a case, which then drives the cost up. If you plan to carry this around, or just to store, you will really want a case. All I can say is that I am very happy with this item, and yes, I would absolutely recommend it!

UPDATE:
There is something that you may experience, which is not a big deal, and is what I have termed clamp 'pop'. The clamps have two pieces on the jaw, one on each side, which move, for helping to grip the backdrop. Sometimes one of these will 'pop' off. While it is slightly annonying, the clamp is not 'broken'. These little pieces have a recessed channel, and will clip back onto the retaining bar, built into the clamp. You need to observe the opposite piece, to see which end needs to be 'up' (which is the FAT end). Don't be in a rush, as you might break it, putting in back in. Just apply firm pressure, in the middle of the piece (so that both sides of the piece are receiving equal pressure), and press it back in.

I have seen some commentary, stating that the clamp 'broke', when they attempted to attach a backdrop. I believe it was this piece coming off, for which they were talking about. Not a world shattering event, and easily fixable.

UPDATE
Ok full story, got tired of those pieces of the clamp popping off. I bought new, all metal clamps, off Amazon--$9.95.

title: Fastest computer I've ever used
text:
What a stunner this lightweight (2.7 lbs) laptop is! With a 1 TB solid state drive, the PC boots up to a usable desktop in under 30 seconds. I dreaded updating WIndows 10 with all the updates that have come out, but the speed of this beauty made quick work of getting me up to date with all the Microsoft and all the Dell updates.

I will only buy computers with SSDs anymore, but there's always the work involved in setting up the SSD for my programs and the hard drive for my data and OneDrive and changing the Documents and Pictures libraries to default to the hard drive. But a one terabyte SSD instead of a small SSD plus a large hard drive is such a more elegant (and expensive) solution. Between the SSD and 16 GB of RAM, this Dell is hands-down the fastest computer I've ever used.

The small screen makes the laptop much lighter and easier to carry around, but I was worried it might be too small for me to read easily. There's almost no bezel around the stunning 4K UHD display to make it look a bit bigger, and the sharpness makes the display surprisingly easy to read. Watching 4K videos is awesome. I typically use my laptops plugged in, but I unplugged this in order to review it. The display stayed very bright for 4 hours and 15 minutes and then dimmed when it went into battery saving mode when the battery level dipped to 10%. The computer was constantly used for the whole time, so if you need to use this for over 4 hours on battery during the day, you'll need to be able to recharge it periodically. It seems to take about 2 to 2 1/2 hours for a full charge.

If you can afford the price and want a beautiful, lightweight, powerful laptop, I can highly recommend this one to you.

title: Sylvania-SKCR271 - Item sent was not the item ordered - photo does not match item
text: The purpose of a 'clock radio' is to be a 'clock' so that you can tell time and a 'radio' which picks up signals of a station and plays the sound. In addition to the photo of the product shown on Amazon not matching the product - one is gray in the photo but what was sent (and returned) is black - the panel which is all black with tiny indications of what to push for what purpose is both hard to see and impossible to negotiate making it, for me, totally inadequate. When I tune to a station, I expect the display to show the various frequencies until I arrive where I want and then revert to showing the clock. This radio never reverts to the clock but rather shows only the frequency - forever. Unhelpful! If you press display, the time will show momentarily but the display quickly reverts to the frequency. When you play a CD, the display shows what cut is playing and how many seconds have passed the whole time the CD is playing never reverting to show the correct time. Whoever designed such a product must have no idea what 'clock radio' means. Whoever thought it a good idea to make black remotes and black face plates for items often in a darkened room along with tiny letters indicating function obviously never used the product they designed or they would have seen the flaws. At first I thought I could live with the inadequacies so I placed white adhesive dots on the faceplate to indicate up and down volume, on and off and display. Then I discovered that the reception at least in my house which has a metal roof was spotty - fading in and out while I was in the shower seemingly dependent on the position of my arm. I looked for a place to attach an external antenna and found none - another reason NOT to buy this product. So here, I have outlined several reasons NOT to buy this product and I am baffled by the good reviews which are posted here which makes me doubt reviews as being authentic. I will reserve my judgement until I see if my review is posted or not. Under 'rate features' do you find it strange that 'reception' is not a quality to be rated? How about 'ease of use'?

title: Unsung hero of the business world-- Latitude laptops! Highly recommended.
text:
I work for an agency of about 200 employees. I handle all the PC's, laptops, and Apple products. About 10 years ago I started buying Latitude laptops for the organization. Since then, the demand for laptops has increased.

The Latitude 7280 comes from a legacy of tough, powerful laptops. The beauty of the L7280 is that it's powerful, very thin, and light. It's also very well built. Dell shaved the weight down under 3 pounds and shrunk the overall depth and chassis. As a result, you have a laptop about the size of a binder and around 3/4" thick that's less than 3 pounds.

The rubberized case gives the feeling of a rugged and non-marking surface. When you start it up, it starts quickly and the screen is bright. I have to use the "night mode" at night otherwise it glares too bright. I have this model and received it with Windows 7 Pro. I upgraded it to Windows 10 Enterprise, added a 250GB drive, and 8GB more memory, so I have 16GB of RAM, 250GB drive that's very fast, and it makes for a very fast little hot rod of a laptop.

If you buy a refurbished model, make sure you go to support.dell.com and enter the service tag on the bottom of the laptop and have the Dell drivers checker check all your drives. Then download Dell Drivers Command, a program that monitors your laptops devices to make sure you have the latest versions.

I foresee using this laptop for one more year and might switch to Dell XPS 13 only because the screen's larger and my eyes are getting older LOL. But for younger eyes, this laptop is a perfect little gem if you know how to set it up. In my opinion it's hard to beat the Dell business line of laptops, even for students. They are made to be scratch resistant, jostled about, and have a rugged finish. This laptop is highly recommended.

title: Who really owns this?
text:
I purchased my Kindle from a brick and mortar on Black Friday 2017. At first, the Kindle ran just fine, and was perfect for what I wanted it to do. Around August of 2018, it started to really slow down, even when I closed all of the apps, or at least thought I had closed all of the apps. Also, about this time, the controls at the bottom would not respond, and not even show up, the power button wouldn't put it into sleep mode but would come back on and show the Amazon ad, and it became absolutely sluggish. I did multiple restores, and called Amazon support 3 separate times, and was told every time someone would get in touch with me to explain what they had found out after downloading my system specs. No one contacted me with any explanation at all, and only once did someone sort of follow up 2-3 months later asking if my Kindle was still working. That’s it.
After doing some research, I learned about the apps running in the background that really impacts the systems performance. More research gave me some info on how to turn some of them off, albeit, only temporarily, to improve performance. It did have some effect, but system is still hampered by all of the apps that cannot be turned off because Amazon needs to collect minute information about you. So, the question is, who owns this Kindle, me or Amazon? It appears that Amazon is the one who owns it because it controls most of what is running in the background, and this effects the system performance. I cannot turn the apps/programs off, and Amazon gets to spy on my every move. I will not purchase another Kindle device, and the one I purchase will probably have as many of the same spy apps running in the background, but better system specs may keep it from becoming bogged down.
It would be great if someone developed a tablet that didn’t spy on you out of the box, one that only ran what was essential, something that only ran what you wanted it to run, something that wasn’t geared toward revenue generation (ie greed). Just a thought.
2/20/19 Forgot to add that the battery is drains very quickly now, even in sleep mode. After 1 1/2 years, the tablet is dying, not sure renting it from Amazon for the original price is worth it.

Addendum:
Shortly after posting my review of the Kindle, Amazon Support called and started to assess my kindle in a more thorough manner. I spoke with three different individuals on three different occasions, mainly due to shift changes, but each one knew what was being discussed concerning my Kindle issues. Indirectly, I learned that my Google installs were the primary culprits of most of my issues, so I didn't reinstall them. Overall, the Kindle performs better, however, the home buttons still freeze at times and the system remains slow, but now I don't have access to the apps and browsers I really like. So the Kindle is performing better, but is not what I need. I will not buy another Kindle, instead, I will purchase a dedicated Android tablet.

Pairing with any device is simple and easy to do. But I get discrepancies of battery life. My PC shows 10% battery life, my phone shows 100%. Which do I believe?

The BT connection is lacking too. I was watching a show on my PC and the headphones disconnected three times. So iffy battery-life and a wacky BT connection, now we're down to 1 star.

For those of you that are wondering if it's my PC that has a goofy BT connection, it's not. I've had other BT headsets and headphones connected without any issues.

Lastly, the instructions say to charge for 4 hours, I've left it overnight, so in theory, the battery should be full / 100% by the time I use them. Maybe the quality control let it pass, I don't know. All I do know is that I wouldn't recommend this product to anyone looking for wireless headphones.

title: Express Keys Troubleshooting
text:
Screen works well with very little parallax after calibration. The screen is fast and responsive, though the lack of instructions could use a bit of work. If you are running a multi monitor set up you'll want to make sure you set the display to accurate reflect where you want it in relation to your other monitors. In my case I select it as monitor 3 and drag it beneath my main screen as my tablet sits in front of my working monitor. For the price, the build quality is excellent. I am honestly happy with the HARDWARE, but the software? Not so much.

The Cons: I purchased a Kamvas Pro 16, and the last "Stable" driver is over a year old, the last two drivers are still marked "Beta" release. However if you look at the product number under the skew my device is a GT-516HDV2, which turns up 4 more drivers. I installed the latest of these drivers on my long road to troubleshooting why my express keys didn't work.

You see I've reprogrammed the keys and through it all I've determined the keys will only respond to the pre-coded check boxes available on the UI. So the keys can be programmed to Mouse Click, Shift, CTRL, and ALT. No other keys or programming combinations / key stroke recordings work. If for instance, you would like to program "Undo" the keyboard shortcut is almost universally Ctrl-Z (and I'm using photoshop where this is the case). I can set the keystroke in the Huion app to output Ctrl-Z, but when you actually fire up photoshop (or anything, notepad for instance) pressing the button ONLY sends the Ctrl command, it is never followed by the Z.

Half the reason I bought the display was for the quick keys, enabling things like zoom, rotate, change brush shortcut, undo, and save. Only, I can't do that now.

So after installing all 7 available drivers , with admin, disabling windows ink, disabling touch, ensuring "software override" for pen input is enabled. I received the tablet on a Friday (Kudos to Amazon logistics) but the ticket I opened with Huion states it will be at least 3-4 days to get a response with potentially longer wait times due to high volume.

So back on my own for troubleshooting. I have multiple workstations so I decided to really troubleshoot. My current PC is an Intel based computer that is definitely personalized. As such I suspected maybe an input driver was fighting for commands. I have a few devices which have programmed macro's and wanted to rule them out. I installed the latest GT516 driver on an AMD workstation that was more bare bones and low and behold it worked.

So back to my intel machine, I rolled back the windows build to before I started this adventure. Then I configured for what would be a "clean boot". After a clean boot the latest GT516 drivers worked and the express key functions took hold.

I then slowly added start up services back into the mix but so far the culprit hasn't returned. As such some of the potential conflicts could be Razer Synapse, iCue, Logitech G-Suite, Nvidia control center. I thought my problems were resolved until, a reboot!

Back to square one, there is some windows or software service that is blocking the PID from transmitting the user string.The good news-ish? Huion support emailed me, but their solution was "Try to re-install the driver".

Final Edit: A Citrix SQL Injection detection client was prevent the input string from being generated. I raised my score to 4 stars. I can't fully rate it five stars, since I had to invest about 5 hours of trouble shooting to make it work. BUT, I have to admit, it does work well for the money now that I have it set up.

title: Great Case!! Buy It! You will Thank Yourself!
text:
This is a Five Star case. The reason I bought this case is because it has a "kick-stand" to support the tablet in a vertical position. You open the kick-stand and it's absolutely stable for use.

I have purchased cases that are broken into segments with no actual stand, but "sort of" holds the tablet using friction between the segments. These are absolutely WORTHLESS. The lightest touch make these cases slide the tablet flat again. Those types of tablet cases are the most annoying ever!!

In contrast, this case positions the tablet nearly vertical for use. It is rock solid when used on your tap or a table. There is never an issue with the tablet accidentally sliding flat as you have with the other poorly designed cases.

I cannot speak to the durability because I have not owned this for long, but it is covered with the PU (man made) "leather" which has a nice look and feel. It seems to be very well made and has a solid feel to it, so I would expect that this case will last for quite some time.

The keyboard is very nice with a good feel. It connects to the tablet quickly without issue. It is almost identical to "Arteck" keyboards that I have purchased many times and LOVE these keyboards. So, if the included keyboard proves to similar to the Arteck, it should last a very long time. There is a frame around the keyboard which touches the frame of the tablet, thus keeping the keys away from the screen when closed. There is NEVER any danger of the keyboard keys touching and damaging the screen, so you are perfectly safe in closing the case with the keyboard installed.

In Summary, I am very happy with this case and keyboard. I would highly recommend it for use with the Samsung Tab S5e.

The only negative is that I believe the purchase price is a little high, but can live with that if this case proves as durable as it seems.

I got these for my Xbox and they look really nice, even better than the pictures on Amazon (which is pretty rare). I got these for my kids, I have a dedicated gaming headset but Im always worried we'll have visitors that may use and break them, so these are meant to be the replaceable, I won't lose a lot of money, type units. If I have any complaint, it is with the headset cable itself, although I haven't had any issues it not uncommon for headset cables to short out, it would have been nice if the cable was replaceable, unfortunately it is not. title: Reasonable value at reasonable price
text:
I'm just getting to know the micro four thirds system and thought at this price, what is there to lose with a 500mm lens. Well keep in mind, that the small m4/3 sensor size effectively doubles your focal length, so this is really a 1000 mm telephoto. That means you need a super steady, smooth tripod to be able to get any view of anything in such a tiny field of view. (I haven't needed to try the doubler obviously and the accessories aren't a lot of help yet, but can't hurt).
The f8 stop is a mixed blessing. Obviously not great for very low light but modern sensors compensate for a lot of sensitivity.
The shot of the baby owl tells the story. This tiny bird is in a nest at least 100' from my camera. The shot is cropped a bit and I had to amp up the color saturation to make up for the weak light transmission.
But the bottom line is I got the shot, a rare shot for me and a difficult one for a very low price. It was tough and a sighting device on the lens would have helped...I might make a simple one. So for a very low lens price I got an impossible shot. I'm searching for a better tripod but needed one anyway.
So that's the trade-off. If you don't want to pay a fortune for a long lens and are well prepared to deal with the shortcomings, you'll get the shot. If you want cinema quality and ease, open your wallet much, much wider.

title: Bought 2 - Perfect for My Specific Needs
text:
Yes, this is a cheap (some would say chinzy) radio but it is just PERFECT for my very specific needs. I was not looking for booming sound quality. I wasn't looking to break the windows of my neighbors' house or even to hear the layered quality of a Mozart concerto. I just wanted a little portable radio to play in the bathroom while I was in the shower and getting ready. Yes, it is likely the plastic "chrome" knobs will chip, and yes, it will not be a family heirloom, but the retro style looks adorable and I get my morning news and background music for an extremely cheap price.

I purchased two because my new house (built in 1966) has a full bath in the hallway and a half bath off what I guess would be called the "master bedroom." I like that it has a cord but also works with batteries. I use the cord to preserve the batteries in case there is a power failure or a natural disaster. Although I wouldn't classify myself as a doomsday prepper (unlike my sister who has a garage full of enough astronaut diapers, airlocked canisters of coffee, non-electric appliances, a fuel generator, and Meals Ready To Eat to feed an army battlion), I do come from Southern California which means earthquakes and fire storms. So compared to my sister's battery powered NOAA/HAM radio system which cost more than my house in Ohio, I feel confident that this little cheap radio just may come in handy. If anything, the cute retro styling will intrigue the zombies during the apocalypse. ; )

Hope this review helps. Let me know if you have any questions.

title: Using for Apple Time Machine and as a long-term SQL Server backup drive - Working great!
text:
My 2-Tb Apple Time Machine drive filled up, and rather than go through the hassle of clearing old backups, I just got this instead. It is FANTASTIC for that purpose. Super-fast and hardly noticeable. The green light is cool, and I like it, but honestly is does it's job "in the background" so I tend to not even notice it. I hadn't noticed any heat issues until the review offered that for rate features. Not noticing any heat really. I shut my Mac down entirely each night, so it isn't on 24/7.

I was so happy with this that I decided to use it for my SQL Server machine. I have about 8 instances of SQL data servers on one machine, each with numerous databases, and I make daily (7 day rotation) and weekly backups (up to 1 year). On one drive, it was filling things up too much. So I got this as a second external SSD, and it's now the weekly backups for all instances and databases. Works great! Hardly noticeable. And I DID pull a backup for a client from 2 weeks ago and it restored really fast. Like my Mac, this Windows 2019 Server shuts down entirely each night (after backups), so it's not on 24/7. Haven't had any issues.

For the price, this drive is fantastic. If it weren't for how quickly technology improves, I'd probably buy a couple of more and stick them in the closet until needed. Great storage solution!

title: Almost great
text:
Lets start this by saying I'm not an audiophile but I do like good sound quality, I'm also not a beginner when it comes to the android os.

The radio got installed into my 2012 Volkswagen Jetta Sportwagen. I commute 130 miles daily and wanted a better sounding Bluetooth transmitter since the module in the MK6 VW leaves a lot to be desired. This unit satsified that need 100%, mp3 files, tune in and Pandora all sound great compared to stock radio. The android OS is pretty stripped down and not very customizable for a standard user. I'm going to explore rooting it to gain more control over it.

A few cons/complaints:
Depending on what model stock radio you have you will need an adapter. In my case I needed ASIN B071HB8KV3. This unit ships from china so for now I am without terrestrial radio. I wouldve preferred to complete the installation all at once but I will now have to open the dash again to get AM/FM radio to work.
I'm having an issue with the time setting. It does whatever it wants even though I've set it to not look for network or GPS time.
Bluetooth connection is a little particular. I don't take calls over Bluetooth and I don't want my phone to ring over the radio when I do get calls. Turning off the call function in my phone disables my ability to stream music. The Bluetooth media player is also very basic. It doesn't transfer album art or scroll longer titles which would be nice to see since its such a large screen.
One of the startup backgrounds was misspelled. (Welcom to Volkswagen)
There is a floating menu button that I havent figured out how to remove. It seems that wherever I move it, its in the way.
The Car Info app is in metric UOM. Cannot find a setting to change it.
Getting your finger into the corners of the touch screen requires a little wrist acrobatics. (Maybe its just me, or the position of the radio in this particular car)

Pros:
Canbus integration was spot on. Car info app is connected to a few parameters of the ECU and gives out pertinent info.
Steering wheel controls work without having to program anything.
VW does not provide an ignition wire in the harness so installing an aftermarket radio requires running an extra wire and losing the RAP feature. This radio functions like oem when you turn off the car.
Park near your house (or use a hotspot) and use the play store to download apps just like a tablet or phone. Its nice to have Sling, Hulu and Youtube.
Video quality is great compared to screen casting on a major brand double din unit.

Overall, for under $200 this radio cant be beat especially for a standard user. Hopefully rooting it will unlock some features and settings for a more advanced user but I wouldn't hesitate to buy it again.

title: Incredible value
text:
I now own two of the ATEM Minis. We create videos for Facebook Live and YouTube. Our first one was set up to bring together the HDMI stream from 3 different consumer grade ( inexpensive ) video cameras and a computer desktop along with a lavalier mic plugged into the back of the mini. The video output is run into a DVR ( Cloner Pro ) via HDMI to record everything and another output goes to another computer ( an older MacBook Pro ) to livestream. All the cams and computer screen are switched in and out with a single touch of a button that includes fades. This setup saves many hours of video editing time and allows the talent to control the cameras without any need for a second person.

I still have a digital video switcher from 20 years ago that mixed two cameras and two mics. It was over $3,000 back then and doesn't do even a fraction of what the ATEM Mini does. I am only surprised that BlackMagic is selling this at such a low price point. It would be a bargain at $600 but they are only asking $295 for it.

Nicely done BlackMagic!

title: Has vrr gamma issues, but only if the games you play have a lot of near black scenes.
text:
Note: when I mention "flight simulator/simulation" I'm not talking about the Microsoft Flight Simulator 2020 specifically.

I bought this TV for pc gaming, specifically flight simulation and dcs world. At first the 48" size was a bit overwhelming coming from 27" monitor but after a week I fell in love with the size and picture quality. All the instruments were perfectly readable and seemed more or less true to actual size because of this relatively large display. Colors were awesome and had no issues with sharpness etc.

Unfortunately, I will have to reassign this TV from being a pc/gaming monitor to just being a TV because of one major flaw that is hardware related as far as I understand.

The problem is that when it is night time in flight simulator, and the frame rate drops too far below 120hz (which is practically all the time due to the nature of a flight simulator) any areas that are dark, like some parts of the cockpit or looking outside at the night sky, where it is not completely black, the black levels on the screen flickers or pulses. You can find out more about the issue if you search for "vrr gamma issues" and it seems LG may or may not be able to fix it with a firmware update. Again this issue isn't present if your fps stays close to 120, the native refresh rate of the TV or if the games you play aren't too dark.

Anyway during the day time in the sim there are no issues at all, and this screen is an absolute immersion dream.

I'll definitely be keeping it around and maybe if LG manages to figure out a firmware fix I might steal it away from the living room and back into my room if I can convince my wife. In the meantime I will have to find another display, perhaps a 43" monitor for my specific purposes for now.

title: Worked Great......at first
text:
I was really excited to get this product. I immediately charged it, paired it with my phone and downloaded the app so that I could get the full experience. I really enjoyed the battery life, call sound quality, and the audio sound quality of the product. Unfortunately, after about 3 months, the headset hung up a call on me for the first time. At first I thought it was the phone carrier and gave it another shot. I took note of the signal strength on the phone the next time it happened. I had a 4 bar signal, so it was NOT the carrier, it was the headset. I reached out to Jabra customer support via email at first and I got a response in a couple of days. I did what they explained I had to do. I removed the device from my phone, downloaded the latest firmware for the device, re-paired it with the phone and I had audio. I was still not ready to use it on a business call for fear that it would drop the call. I used it to play videos or Pandora as I was working out. It would stop a video in the middle for no reason, and I would have to start it up again. The same thing happened with Pandora, stopping a song in the middle of it and then I would have to re-start Pandora from the phone. Since I had good response from the website previously, I replied back to the original message. and included my ticket number in the reply. After 3 weeks, I have yet to hear back from them. Today, I called the customer service number and am on hold while I am writing this review. It took them 27 minutes to answer the call, but FINALLY KIM was excellent and was able to help solve my problem. She was able to send me a warranty form via email, and I replied with my proof of purchase and a picture of the device . Once this is filled out and reviewed by the warranty team, they will send me a pre-paid label to return the old device. Once that device is checked in, they will order the replacement for me. I can plan on spending 3 weeks waiting for the new headset. Hopefully the next one will work better.

UPDATE - the warranty form only worked on my iphone, not on the computer in IE, CHROME, or FIREFOX.

4/16/19 - I received my replacement headphones today. They are the 65e version, which was a nice surprise. From the time I sent the old one in until I received the new ones, it was 3 weeks. I have charged them up and am now ready to use them. These have a noise cancellation feature in them, so that will be a new feature to experiment with.

title: These are a MUST HAVE for your Echo Show!
text:
I finally got my first Amazon Echo Show with Alexa. I am kicking myself for not getting one earlier! I have fell in love with these devices and their many capabilities that I bought a dot, 2 Echo Show 5’s an Echo Show 8 and the new Echo Show 8HD! I am loving all the things they do. If you don’t have one and you’re on the fence here is the breakdown, pros and cons:
Breakdown: super SUPER easy to use. Plug in the power cord and follow the on screen steps to set up your device to your liking. There are multiple clock faces to choose from, sounds for alerts and you can pick a background or use your photos from Amazon’s photo app. (I also was new to that app and Alexa. Both were super easy to use! My pictures synced faster than any other photo cloud storing app hands down. Plus as a bonus you don’t need to pay for storage. There’s no limit and zero fees!!)

Once you’ve set up the Alexa app (I recommend the Smart Life app that’s compatible with smart devices/plugs and Apple Watch!) you just ask Alexa what you need and boom, it’s done! I asked her to calm down my dog and she put on music! I am amazed. You can make shopping lists (No more searching for a pen and paper in my kitchen), Ask for recipes, play videos, surf the Internet, find out the weather, watch your photo albums, make phone calls to anyone who has the same type of device (like most of the world does by now). It’s seamless and I even had my 8 year old set one up because it was so easy. I love the parental control platform it allows for too!

Pros:
Super easy to set up
Beautiful looking with or without the swivel base
Amazing picture
Great compatibility with phones, smart plugs, Works perfectly with smart devices and apps
Better than FaceTime for video calls
Loud speakers with excellent sound quality
Alexa, Alexa, Alexa! Alexa’s voice recognition is so much better than Siri! Siri can’t understand a thing I say (I don’t even have an accent). If I ask Siri for the weather it gives me traffic. Super frustrating. I think that’s why I was hesitant at getting one of these. Man I wish I knew how much better Alexa is! Everything I ask is instantly understood and taken care of!! Music, calls, drop ins, weather...anything!
The value for the price is unbeatable
Everything about this device is a Pro!!

Cons:
It’s constantly listening. But honestly, I don’t worry about that. I’m sure the government listens in and sees things just through WiFi, the Nelson rating TV system, Arbitron ratings in your radios, computer cameras and cellular/mobile devices. This isn’t the only thing out there and really it’s so worth it for everything you can use it for. Besides, anyone that paranoid about what they’re saying is probably on The Hunt with John Walsh. LOL

The final analysis: BUY THESE DEVICES!! Get them for each room. Enjoy the capability to make your day to day life easier and more fun! Play music, dance and sing and be silly. Display your photos, try a new recipe and make sure that your prepared for rain, snow or heat. The Echo devices are like having a personal assistant that’s holding a computer screen. So enjoy your new found “tech” if you don’t already have any and you’ll be amazed like me at what these devices can do!

The swivel base is a must have as well. You can move and tilt the screen to suit your needs which makes video calls and cooking from online recipes a breeze!!

title: completely satisfied!!!
text:
I was a bit hesitant about purchasing this antenna as I had previously purchased a flat indoor antenna before from another brand and it was garbage, barely picked up any channel and did not work. I decided to order this after extensive research and reading reviews on the item. I live about 30 miles away from all the towers and with previous indoor antennas, I was able to easily pick up UHF channels no problem but i was never able to get any VHF channels even though those towers were the same distance away. To add on to my predicament, the room where I have my television set up has one window that faces South while all the satellite towers were to the Northeast so I feared the only way I would ever be able to receive VHF channels is to install an outside antenna on my roof. I am no handyman and didn't want to make a big project out of this so I took a chance on this item and I am so glad I did. At first I tried placing the antenna as high on the wall as I could on the Northeast corner of my room since everything I read online kept reiterating that the antenna should be facing the direction of the towers, it was only able to pick up 65-70 channels, none of which were VHF so at this point I was becoming less and less optimistic that this antenna was any different than the ones before but then I decided to place the antenna high on that south window despite knowing it was the complete opposite direction to the towers and unbelieveably the antenna was able to pick up 138 channels, the two VHF channels i wanted (ABC and FOX) were both working with crystal clear reception. Even with the 15 ft cable, i still had to purchase an extender but easy fix and with the extender cable, reception was not compromised at all. Highly highly
recommend this Winegard antenna, its affordable and really does what it advertises to do. I almost purchased an expensive antenna thinking it could do a better job but the little antenna proved me wrong! Honestly the best purchase I’ve made this year thus far.

title: Time will tell, but for now: A+.
text:
Naturally apprehensive about throwing my lot in with Chinese manufacturing when it comes to essential components, especially when they potentially pose fire hazards, I took a chance with this unit. Thus far, a scant 4 days into it, I must say that I'm pleased as punch.

There are a few off-putting aspects here, such as the cheap stickers designating what is what on the panel, and a rather generic feel to the whole affair, but the look and feel is solid on the whole. The cables that come with it are a bad idea, for sure. A 3kw 24v inverter, properly speaking, should be wired with 2/0 on a 175a DC breaker for regular duty applications. I might even go a high as 4/0, 250a if my intended use was to Max this thing out frequently. Using the doubled up 4awgs provided falls a fair bit short of the universally recommended guidelines. I'm also not a fan of lug terminals that hand tighten with plastic knobs, though the connection feels secure enough. No remote I/0 port for a simple toggle switch kinda stinks. That being said:

This inverter does what it says it does. At least to the extent I've tested it so far. Really, is sole function is to kick a submersible ⅓hp 110v 2 wire pump on. This pump runs ~1.1kw ac and pulls an average of 39 DC amps at the battery. This is hardly making big demands on the rating of the inverter, but due to their nature, these pumps come with surge demands that are particularly high, typically 6-7X the rated running capacity. This was my big concern going into it, and I am very pleased to find that this inverter handles that surge without breaking a sweat (about a half second blip on the over current alarm). I've also used it to run a 15a table saw through the rear GFIC outlet, which it did without complaint.

I cannot comment on the charger or ac input side of things, as I already have a nice charger well suited in size to my battery bank. In truth, for the same money, I'd rather have a simple LF inverter without all the other features, but alas, they seem to not exist anywhere at the 3+kw level. Still, considering the options out there, for the $650, this inverter is impossible to overlook. Your normal high quality options (Samlex, Magnum, Outback, Cotek, Go Power, etc) are easily 2-3 times that cost, with surge ratings measured in the milliseconds, rather than seconds (which are likely "governer" type safety features via microprocessors). Again, for the money, I couldn't be happier. Considering it's able to fulfill the essential duties required of it without a hitch, the previous gripes become so minor as to be inconsequential.

It's fairly quiet, and even running the well pump, I've yet to see either fan come on. The limited info on the ac screen is pretty accurate, from what I can deduce. Comparing it with the DC display via my midnite classic 150 appears damn close to right on the money, factoring the rated efficiency rating, tare and conversion losses, etc. Not terrible indeed, for a $10 add on.

To be sure, I'm one of those guys that likes to give scathingly negative reviews when they are well earned, which it seems far too great a ratio of products seem to elicit these days, but once in a great while, I get to write something positive like this. Thanks Solinba and Lin energy. Now only time will tell if you get to keep these accolades.

title: This is a joke, right?
text:
I purchased this specifically for the audio spectrum part so that I could monitor how much power (based on frequencies) was being fed through my Rockville PA amp to my Rockville PA speakers and the separate sub speakers.

THERE IS NO ACTUAL 'AUDIO SPECTRUM ANALYZER' and it is false advertising that Rockville claims such a thing. As at least one other reviewer had posted, the display simply shows a set pattern of LEDs that light up based on the volume of the entire signal and NOT specific frequencies. To give you an example, the 'spectrum analyzer' would display the exact same set of LEDs for a bass drum sound as it would for the sound of a piccolo. In short, what Rockville is claiming to be an 'audio spectrum analyzer' is simply a line level display with 13 rows of lights. Another joke about this unit that is that if it doesn't pick up a signal, it just goes into this cute demo mode where the lights go up and down the display.

While I know Rockville sells cheap (or budget level equipment to be kind), but this is such false advertising that I will be reporting this to Amazon.

title: Great Budget Speedbooster
text:
I'm using this little Speedbooster for my Blackmagic Pocket Cinema Camera 4K. I love how the crop factor compared to full frame decreased from 1.9x or 2x with the 4/3 sensor, to about 1.33x with the Speedbooster. I am used to shooting on APS-C cameras, and this gets me a little wider shots with the same lenses, without being drastically different to what I'm used to.

The fit onto my BMPCC4K is snug, and there is little to no wiggling around, except a very tiny bit of rotational play, which is mildly annoying when zooming/focusing with stiffer lenses, but not really noticeable in the image most cases. It feels solidly constructed.

I mainly use manual lenses, but the electronics do allow me to control the aperture on my Canon lenses, and the display even takes into account the equivalent aperture based on the speedbooster.

I haven't successfully used any autofocus or image stabilization features on my Canon lenses with this adapter yet, and my BMPCC4K doesn't seem to recognize that image stabilization is available at all for Canon lenses. However, I read in a forum that a firmware update of the speedbooster could enable image stabilization with my camera.

Unfortunately, there is no way to use Canon EF-S lenses with this speedbooster - they are designed for a 1.6x crop factor anyway, and wouldn't look right on the equivalent of a 1.3x crop. But because of the longer flange distance of EF-S lenses, they will not physically fit this speedbooster - or many other EF mount adapters in general. Just keep that in mind, as you plan what gear you're purchasing.

One neat trick I've done is to use EF macro tubes (with electronic contacts) on my EF-S lenses, which allows them to be used with the speedbooster and maintain electronic aperture control. You lose the distance/infinity focus because of the macro tubes, but the EF-S lenses will work for specific situations with this setup.

The one problem I've had is that I can't really use any of my lenses wide open - Rokinon primes, Rokinon Cine DS Primes, adapted Tamron Nikon-mount zooms - they all have a lot of "bloom," where the lighter parts of the image appear hazy and never quite in focus when the lenses are at their widest apertures. But stopping down a little clears this problem up, and with the ISO capability of my BMPCC4K, I am not quite as concerned about the loss of light from stopping down a bit.

The build quality is quite nice - the optics of the speedbooster lens(es) inside the adapter are quite sharp and don't degrade the image much to my eye. If you are having problems achieving infinity focus using this adapter, the glass elements inside can be carefully rotated to adjust their distance from the lens/image sensor. This can be done with careful fingers, no tools required.

Overall, this is a great budget alternative to a Metabones speedbooster!

title: Very impressed!
text:
To set the tone I will state for the record I am an avid Leupold optics fan! If leupold makes it and I have a need for it it’s going to Leupold for myself. Their quality and service is next to none! Having said that......

My first pair of Leupold binos were the BX-1 Yosemite’s and they were very, very underwhelming. They were chunky, had poor colour, clarity, and blurred near the edges of the glass. I got them on a great sale but they were returned very shortly; oh and at the time they didn’t come with the awesome case they do now.

I spent a good amount of time and effort looking at reviews, specs, and trying out binoculars in store (even considered other brands after being so disappointed with the previous purchase) before I settled on the BX-2 Acadia’s.

The Acadias are leaps and bounds better then the Yosemite’s I had for a short period of time. The glass is crystal clear, colour fantastic, and they are clear from edge to edge! The rubber exterior is fantastic and will afford good grip even in inclement weather. They eye cups are easily adjusted and stay in place, the lens caps hold firm, adjustments are easily made and knobs have a good resistance to them to help with precision adjustments and prevent accidental rotation.

They also have the ability to mount to a tripod using a threaded adapter that screws in to the front of the swivel hinge; a handy feature to have.

I was not able to ascertain any difference between these and much more expensive binoculars (even higher end Leupolds) and it’s in the sweet spot for pricing as far as I’m concerned. I’m sure there would be an appreciable difference if comparing these to the more expensive pairs when at dawn / dusk when lens coatings and design features make a difference.

The added bonus of getting the binocular case is nice, it saves from having to purchase a separate decent case. The case is sturdy and of high quality quality, the elastic pull to open and close it is a smart idea that many companies have adopted; although in my opinion the pull came installed upside down (quick fix) and it functions better now than it did since changing it.

My only two complaints are that the Acadias are a bit heavier than similar binoculars, and if your counting ounces it might matter to you, if not your good to go.
The second being that I wish the Acadias also came with the Go Afield binocular harness (Leupold part # 172543) as it allows you to mount the binocular case on your chest which is where they are handiest if birding or hunting. As it comes the case has a Molle attachment that they say you can mount over your belt or to a pack strap.

To sum it up I would not recommend the BX-1’s to even my worst enemy; however the BX-2 Acadia’s are a wonderful piece of kit that I would be happy paying much more for them then I did!

title: An honest re-review of the 4K version
text:
Last month (December 2018), I decided to spend some money on myself. Those with kids can understand that feeling or even need. I upgraded my video game systems to a PS4 Pro and Xbox One X, I also upgraded the video card in my PC to be able to handle 4K. I bought this monitor to use with the PS4 Pro, Xbox One X and PC. I originally posted a 5 star review after using it for just one night (Christmas Eve). I did put in my review that I would be back to add to the review as I used it but was going out of town for 2 weeks. I was really impressed with the picture quality. It looked especially good on the Xbox One X games that use HDR. But I hadn't used it that much.

Once back from the holiday visits to family, I was able to use the monitor also with my PC and to see how well my initial very positive reaction to it was holding up. I have to add this to make what I'm going to say make more sense. I had been using a Samsung 32" Smart Television, it was one of the higher end ones with the upgraded speakers, 3 HDMI ports, 1080p max, so it wasn't a pushover. Once I got settled in with this Viewsonic, I started wondering why I kept leaning forward to change the settings. I kept looking for a remote control. Then, as if a higher power, computer deity was looking down, my PC's speakers (Harmon Kardon Soundsticks) stopped working. That's not a surprise as they were my third set in 5 years. I switched the sound from the speakers to this monitor.

The sound this monitor produces might be the worst I've ever heard. I was playing Madden 19, the crowd sounded like they were inside a garbage can, two blocks from my house. It was like a version of white noise. I turned the master volume on the monitor up to 100 but still could only understand about half of what the announcers said. I started messing with the settings thinking there had to be a way to make the speakers sound better but there wasn't. This also reminded me of how nice a remote would be with this monitor.

When you change the settings, the buttons are little thumb buttons on the back left side of the monitor. Meaning, you can't see which one you're pushing. They sort of "fixed" that by having the buttons show up on your screen but there's six of them. If you're aiming for one, you pretty much have to let your finger slide down them until you get to the 3rd or 4th one that you need to press. It could close before you get it done. And each menu has up to 3 levels. Meaning, you press the "enter/okay" button on what you're looking for and it opens a new menu. The six buttons change from up/down to left/right depending on which menu you're in.

You're welcome to look over my 14 years of reviews here at Amazon and see how easily I'm annoyed by something simple being made complex. Within a week, I hated this monitor. Sure, the picture quality is really great but I didn't like anything else about it. It even has a power block that you have to plug in to your outlet. And don't forget the sound/speakers. Maybe I was expecting too much out of it since I did have a PC, Xbox One X and PS4 Pro hooked up to it but my 32" Samsung television has no problem handling all 3.

That adds one more annoyance. I'm sure someone will tell me to buy a HDMI splitter with remote but I expect a product this expensive to not need an add-on to be easy to use. You also have to go through those menus just to switch from HDMI 1 to HDMI 2 to Display Port. Go ahead, tap the wrong button and it will mess your settings up and you have to do this every time you want to switch to say the Xbox One X instead of the PC. I really believe a remote would make a ton of difference in this monitor and better speakers would help too. I realized it didn't have a remote when I first started to switch between the PC and Xbox One X. My wife thought it was hilarious. I looked at the screen and said, "I have no idea how you change the input." Looked in the box, questioned my puppy about eating it then just accepted there's no remote. I sit about 30 inches away from the monitor, meaning, I'm not sitting right up at the desk it sits on. So, to change the settings/inputs, I have to get up and reach behind the monitor. Call that lazy if you will but I'm around 40 and work 8-12 hours a day. Meaning, maybe a kid, a teenager who likes changing settings and seeing the results, would be perfectly fine with this monitor. But I can't say I am. Luckily, I kept my Samsung television and just hooked it back up for the meantime. It's not capable of the picture quality of this monitor but it does everything else better and much easier. Not to mention, it was only half the price of this monitor. I can't justify the price for what I would call a 25% improvement in picture quality with a complete drop-off in functionality.

Last, I will recommend this monitor, as long as you're not bothered by the parts that annoyed me. It's very well made, the stand is excellent, very easy to attach, the monitor can be raised and lowered on the stand, tilted, rotated. As said the picture quality is excellent too. Overall, it's why I gave it 4 stars. It's just not for me. I don't think the features ratings show on reviews, so here's what I gave this monitor. A 5 star out of 5 on picture quality. A 3 star out of 5 for gaming, others will also mention its response rate not being that great in fast-paced video games. A 2 out of 5 for value for money. I explained that above when talking about my Samsung television doing everything better for half the price.

title: So far so good
text:
Finally mounted the antenna outdoors a couple days ago and here is my updated review.
Mounting the pole was fairly simple as long you have the right tools to do it. I decided to mount it about 20 feet above ground on the side of my house. I ended up using my power drill with masonry drill bits to drill holes through a stucco, inserted plastic screw anchors, and used a torque wrench to secure the bolts.
The mounting bracket that came with the pole is more than sufficient and allows the pole to adjust up/down.
I wish the pole was a little longer though.
Attaching the antenna unit itself on the pole is a no brainer. Just make sure to secure both the turn-knobs and your set.
I also made sure there is enough cable to allow for the unit to turn as it is a rotating antenna.
I used the splitter to allow for multiple TVs to connect.
So far, I'm able to see all the local channels plus other channels with most at HD quality on all three TVs connected to the antenna.
Recommendations:
If this is going to be a DIY project, I highly suggest you ground the antenna. I purchased from Amazon the following to do this: copper grounding wire, and a coaxial ground block. This will run you about $20 but it's worth it in case of a power surge or lightning strike. There are plenty of short clips or instructions available on the Web.
Another item I ended up buying is a coax cable stripper and crimper kit (ran me about $15 on Amazon). I found some of my coax cables are missing the connectors.
Overall I spent about $100 for everything. Was it worth it? I think so. It's definitely much less for what I will pay the cable company on channels that I normally watch. Now I can watch my favorite local news, primetime shows, late night shows, even cultural documentaries/shows that I find interesting.
I will keep my preliminary review below.

This is a preliminary review.
(1) Packaging - parts were properly packaged. No missing or broken items.
(2) Unit assembly - there is some assemble required but was simple. Instruction was straight forward. The included long coax cable was a plus for me.
(3) Product quality - the antenna unit itself is made of plastic and aluminum. It feels sturdy and with the accompanying metal pole and wall bracket, i think it should withstand heavy winds. Not sure yet if it will last long enough from the sun's exposure.
(3) Pre-test - before I start mounting the antenna outdoors, I placed the assembled unit on a table indoors just to test the unit is working. So far, I can get at least 5 channels that are crystal clear without any interference.
As soon the rain storm clears up, I'll start mounting the unit up on the roof and will post another review. By then, I hope to get more clear channels. Will also post my review of the rotation feature of the unit.

Update: after multiple home base reboots and doorbell "rejoins" I got this to work. I probably spent a good 5 or 6 hours working on this thing to get it to work. I should have just returned it, it's not worth that much hassle. So after a few months of relatively good experience, except for the fact I only get about six days of battery life, the home base quit chiming on the press of the doorbell button. I checked all settings to no avail. I think the speaker or related electronics in the home base simply failed. After another wasted hour, I decided to integrate the eufy with my Amazon Echo for the chime in addition to my smartphone. Problem solved, but it's not such a good showing for Anker/eufy. I think the product is shoddy at best.

--- Original review----

The packaging and the initial setup of the homebase was exceptional. But unfortunately that's where the positives ended in my experience with this product. After charging the doorbell and adding it to the home base, problems began. First, it is very hard to snap into the mount. The bottom kept springing out. I mounted the thing properly by the way - not my first rodeo. Ultimately I found I had to press upward and to the right of the mount to make it click into place. Not great, but not such a big deal.

I tested the doorbell button and heard the chime from the homebase, cool. Tried again a minute later and... Nothing. No chime, no motion detection, no video recording. The doorbell just up and died. But not exactly. It seemed to sort of stay manageable in the app, but any time I tried to change a setting, I'd get an error message, something like "close failed" and "open failed". Trying to view the couple clips recorded of myself installing the doorbell resulted in a "cannot connect to doorbell (-204)" error. Tried eufy's "help" - that's a joke. Tried support chat, sorry they're closed.

I think it's a signal problem, but it shouldn't be. Homebase is on WiFi, but tests "great", whatever that means. I tested -47 dBm on 2.4Ghz and -52dBm on 5Ghz. No nearby interferers. So yeah, my WiFi is pretty good. As for the distance between the doorbell and the home base? About 9 feet horizontally and 2 vertical feet. I couldn't find info about how close to each other they need to be, but it seems like 10 linear feet should be a reasonable distance.

I tried deleting and re-adding the doorbell to the homebase, which was successful and once again recorded me having a hard time snapping back into the mounting bracket, but again, that was the only time it did anything. Same errors, this time it also said it was "offline". Deleting and adding a third time, same thing. Rinse and repeat.

I'm pretty frustrated at this point, but I may waste some more of my time playing with this piece of junk before I box it back up for a return.

title: Philips BDM4350UC vs. ordinary 43" 4k TV
text:
This is the first time that I started out writing a positive review, but then my own review convinced me to return the item.

TL;DR If you need to simultaneously display images from multiple computers, the Philips BDM4350UC is good. If you want to display just one computer at a time, an ordinary 4k TV is just as good and much more economical.

I work mostly with text and simple diagrams. I use lots of large windows and I dislike the seam between the company-provided dual monitors. So I bought my own 43" 4k monitor to use at work.

This is my second 43" monitor; at my last company I used a 43" Samsung 4k TV [[https://www.amazon.com/Samsung-Electronics-Smart-LED-UN43NU6900FXZA/dp/B07F1T4JFB/]]. I found both the Samsung and Philips monitors quite satisfactory for my kind of work.

Other reviewers complain of unusual phenomena at the edge of the screen, dead pixels and burn-in. I see none of these problems in my Philips BDM4350UC.

Advantages of Philips BDM4350UC:
DisplayPort, HDMI and VGA inputs
Displays 1, 2, 3 or 4 inputs as once
Picture-in-picture display
Matte display surface reflects less room light
The monitor automatically figures out what to do; you don't so much need a remote control
No smart TV functionality to get in the way

Disadvantages of Philips BDM4350UC:
Automatic scanning for the active input takes time, resulting in an annoying delay upon wake up
Automatic scanning for the active input may choose an input different from the one you want to view
When the monitor sleeps, the USB hub sleeps. Thus you cannot wake the computer using the keyboard or mouse connected to the hub. So I don't use the hub.
No remote control; must reach for the on-screen display joystick on the back panel
Much more expensive than a 4k TV

Advantages of an ordinary 4k TV:
Stays on the same input until you change it; no waiting for the monitor to find the active input
Includes a remote control
It's also a TV
Dramatically lower price

Disadvantages of an ordinary TV:
Glossy screen intended for a dark room, not a brightly lit office
After the input goes inactive, TVs turn off assuming you are done watching TV. I want my monitor to sleep, ready to be awakened when I resume work.
No DisplayPort or VGA inputs

After writing this review I decided that I do not need the multiple input abilities of the Philips BDM4350UC. I'm getting an ordinary TV for less than half the price, probably an LG 43UM7300 recommended by the rtings site.

title: More powerful than the 5/6 fan setups, pay attention to CFM ratings!
text:
I intially ordered a 6 fan laptop cooler that had way more reviews than this one, many more positive reviews as well, for my HP Spectre Folio (3 years old, horrible overheating issues, already tried cleaning). I then came to realize that many of the reviews appeared to be fake. When I received that product, one of the fans started making a grinding sound after about 1 hour and one of the red LEDs stopped working. So, yeah, I returned that piece of junk.

I then spent more time than is healthy trying to find a laptop fan that wasn't just "cool" looking and would actually make a difference. So, I started scouring the internet for this important measurement: CFM. The rated CFM for this fan from the manufacturers website is 76.5 maximum (has variable speed knob). That CFM rating is one of the highest I could find in this price range after all my research, though there were laptop fans released 7/8+ years ago that were higher.

Another reason why I settled on this one is b/c I've owned the CoolerMaster X-Slim for about 4/5 years now and the fan on it still works flawlessly, even after I would purposefully abuse it sometimes (force stopping the fan, etc.). That models CFM rating is 70 CFM and I don't like how the USB plug is built-in to it. The wire on mine started to short, so the fan was becoming unreliable unless I jiggled the wire quite a bit.

Back to the product I'm actually reviewing...

Pros:
1.) High CFM for price (76.5)
2.) Doesn't have an annoying built-in cord, meaning I can swap out cords as they become old, then just plug them in like any other USB device
3.) Variable speed knob
4.) The LED light is cool, though I don't use it.
5.) Extra USB slot for another device
6.) IMPORTANT: I've watched countless review videos of people holding paper over their fan to see if the airflow would move it. This one's airflow DOES lift paper, so it will actually have a use beyond just being a cool looking paperweight with an LED. I tested this with notebook paper, toilet paper, and a paper towel. All three were lifted by the airflow.

Cons:
1.) The front fan vent that "keeps your hands dry" is more for looks than anything. When I place paper over it, it actually seems like it's pulling air in, not blowing it out. It's a non-issue for me, and I guess that technically, any air movement would keep one's hands dry.
2.) Would be amazing if they added a 2nd open USB slot to add two additional devices
3.) I would have preferred USB-C instead of micro-USB. Again, not much of an issue me for me.

I hope this review was helpful for everyone frustrated over the junk and marketing for most of these laptop "cooling" fans, most of which do absolutely nothing at all, or breakdown prematurely.

title: KEF hits another home run - close to the $2k LS50 system for half the price!
text:
This gets amazingly close to their state-of-the-art LS50 powered system which is probably the best small amplified speaker system ever made – but at $2K, the LS50 has a price to match, while the LSX has about 95% of its big brother's DNA for only 50% of its price. Relative to its bigger brother, the LSX shows only a modest reduction in built-in amplifier power (and probably something like ~3 db in terms of max volume levels), with somewhat less reach into the lower bass fundamentals below 60 Hz, and a bit less cabinet volume, but with a more streamlined and more pleasantly styled cabinet in the LSX. The LSX system realistically does not have much bass below ~50 Hz but, mitigating this, its midbass is excellent and very articulate, making it very easy to follow any bass line or instrument in your music selection.

Speaking of selection, it appears that almost all the negative reviews around this system relate to difficulty people have with either connecting it to streaming or some other aspect of its streaming software – not with the audio quality of the speakers – which are simply phenomenal. I think you'd be hard-pressed to find small pair of speakers that sound as good, and outside of KEF's own LS50 systems (powered or otherwise), in my opinion, there isn't one.

It's not perfect however, and I would dock KEF for their failure to duplicate at least the basics of the control architecture of the remote on the back panel of the master speaker – this leaves you with an inability to turn the system out of its suspended or sleep mode without the remote control. If you lose your remote control or it becomes inoperative (which is going to happen to more than a few users, given how often this system is likely to be placed outdoors on patios and lanais and thereby potentially exposed to moisture at least accidentally), you cannot either turn the system on from suspend, or adjust volume, except through your Bluetooth source. Re-initializing the system by unplugging it still brings the system up in a suspended mode. We may attempt to secure a second remote control from KEF. Also one has to admit to the somewhat buggy nature of some of their apps. However, since we drive the speakers exclusively from a Bluetooth source streaming lossless files, potentially buggy interactions with streaming software are a nonissue.

Pros:

1) Superb tonal balance and neutrality, including remarkable fidelity on vocal material, consistent with virtually all of KEF's recent high-end designs
2) excellent bass, given small cabinet size and one half cost of state-of-the-art LS 50 powered system
3) with decent subwoofer the LSX becomes relatively inexpensive full range system with very small footprint
4) attractive range of colors to match room interiors (plus the white color no longer contains a hideous copper driver seen in LS 50)

Cons:

1) you're SOL if you lose the remote or it becomes nonfunctional
2) Streaming app can be a chore to get operating properly
3) not much else to complain about

In summary, it's a nearly perfect small compact system for small to medium-size rooms and spaces, it will play decently loud, and it is an exceptionally faithful and accurate transducer. If you've got a high quality source, it can approach a state-of-the-art system for way less than state-of-the-art money, especially with the addition of a decent subwoofer.

title: Serious Design Flaw, Poor Customer Service
text:
This was originally a five-star review, headlined "Well-Designed, Good-Sounding." It turns out this product has a serious design flaw, a problem that the manufacturer/seller is unwilling to properly address under warranty. First, here is my original review:
----------

An under-the-chin, stethoscope-type pair of earphones is my choice for certain listening applications, and these fit the bill perfectly. They are comfortable in extended use, and sound quality is actually quite good... which is to say I was expecting average and these outperformed.

Don't want loose-fitting earbuds that keep falling out? Don't want tight-fitting earbuds that you have to shove into your anatomy? Traditional over-the-head or wacky behind-the-neck stereophones not the answer? Then give these a try. They provide a modicum of acoustic isolation with a pleasant, neutral spectral response.

I'm quite happy with them.
----------

Now, for the problem. Before even a full month of use, one of the foam ear tips deteriorated and partially broke off. I contacted the seller by email. Their response was essentially that this was an expected occurrence and that I should buy a 5-pair set of replacement ear tips for a price equal to the original purchase cost of the headphones. I checked this out, and sure enough: The original purchase price of the headphones was $16.99; the 5-pair set of replacement ear tips is $16.99.

I think you can see what's going on here. How do you pull off a doubling of purchase price on unsuspecting customers? Build in a design flaw that requires the purchase of an equally priced remedy.

If Simolio is serious about being a "quality" brand, the proper course of action here would be to provide free replacement ear tips to customers under warranty (as Sennheiser did for me with their under-chin headphones) or to provide, perhaps, a neoprene or silicone option that holds up better under regular use. As it is, it seems they are running a scam.

So, buyer be warned.

(P.S. - I have been offered a 50 percent discount on the purchase of replacement ear tips.)

(P.P.S. - I see this product listing has been updated with a different item -- headSET {with mic} -- that includes extra foam ear tips. Also $16.99! Fine, but that does not address my problem.)

title: Stupid Camera and Pathetic Customer Service
text:
It gives me absolutely no pleasure to write a bad review. I very rarely do it. But my frustration level with this camera requires me to do so. I bought the camera in June 2016. In their defense, I will say that it is easy to set up, and despite my star ratings, the actual appearance of the camera, i.e., the picture it delivers, is fine, not what I would consider high definition (my iPhone is better)...but much better than the make-believe camera that came built in with my HP laptop.

My main gripe about this camera is that the image is reversed, which makes working with it beyond frustrating, especially when streaming conferences. Why in the world would they do that. In other words, if I look at the imagine displayed on my laptop's screen, the wall on my right is on my left, instead of staying on my right. That is the "stupid" part of my review headline. Why would they do that?!

The "pathetic customer service" part of my headline is that I have been trying for years to find a way to fix this. There are YouTube videos that talk about fixing it, but they have different software than what came from the company and they also mention that you have to drop the quality from 1080 down to 480. Really?! Then what is the purpose of buying a 1080 camera.

Also, I saw a post on Logitech's support site that addressed this precise question. The user stated that there used to be a box that could be checked that could turn mirroring on and off but that it no longer works.

I can tell you that with the software that Logitech provided, there isn't even a box that can be checked. By the way, that question (above) on the support site by the other person, that was written four years ago, and Logitech never followed up with a complete answer. They just ignored the person...you know, the customer.

INTERPRETATION: Yea, we know we have a problem with the camera, but, frankly, we just don't care...you see, we are a big company and you're nothing to us.

SOLUTION: Never buy another Logitech product again. Eventually companies like this go out of business. They truly do. No customers; no business. They have lost their way, so find your way to another company

FINAL THOUGHT: You clowns out there who are trying to gouge the Amazon customer by taking a $79 product and trying to sell it for $250 or more because of the Covid-19 crisis should be ashamed of yourselves. Karma can be a real kick in the head.

title: DIFFICULT REMOVAL FIX
text:
First off, I did not read the reviews of this product since it was an add-on to the Striker 4 Fish Finder made by the same company. I assumed it would fit nice, look good, and there would be no issues.

It’s a great cover made entirely of hard plastic and it fits the Striker 4 (not the plus model). It actually fits so well that you would never want to take it off, because you literally can’t. I cannot imagine the struggle it takes for kayak fisherman to get this cover off while they’re out in the water. I have a 14ft boat that’s kind of tippy and I could only get this cover off by removing the fish finder from the mount itself. It’s an unnecessary hassle that takes away from any day out fishing.

Now a lot of people say to file down the little plastic lips that “clip” the cover onto the fish finder, but it sucks damaging a brand new product. So I found an INCREDIBLE solution that works. All you need is a little piece of wood (or whatever hard material you prefer) and some tape. In my photos you can see that the piece of wood is taped on the bottom part of the cover and that it has a snug fit between the two little plastic lips that clip to the fish finder.

The goal here is to simply prevent the clipping action from taking place because that’s what makes it so difficult to remove. By adding this little piece of wood to the bottom, the cover will only slide onto the fish finder instead of clip. It also won’t slide off easily because it’s a really tight fight and overall it just makes it 10x easier to remove. In order to remove, you just put one hand on the back of the fish finder (for support) and then lift off the cover by the bottom with your other hand.

That’s the best solution I could think of. And if it doesn’t work for some odd reason, you’re not really out anything because it’s just some tape and a piece of wood. The cover itself isn’t damaged in any way, so it’s definitely worth trying.

title: I really wanted to like this watch, but I can't.
text:
I would not recommend this product. Rarely have I ever given only 2-stars for any product.
My son gave me this ZeTime Petite watch for Christmas ’19, and I’ve been frustrated with it ever since, starting on Day 1 when it took the whole day and night for it to fully charge. About the only thing I really like about it is you can create your own watch face, but I had to figure out how to put the different elements where I wanted them – the directions that came with the watch didn’t tell me. The first thing that frustrates me is the inconsistency of the display not turning on when I flick my wrist over to see the time. And something that really frustrates me is the charging. Last Sunday night, I put the watch on the charger because it was at 19%. The next morning, more than seven hours later, it was only at 54%; and that evening, it had made its way up to only 94%! And yes, I know it was charging all that time because it emits a high pitch sound (another irritating thing) when the watch is sitting properly on the charger. And for MyKronoz to say that this watch could go up to 30 days on a single charge is absolutely flat out wrong! The battery level was at 40% when I left this watch on my dresser for two days (the display is set to not come on unless there is movement). So even though it had not been moved for two whole days, on the evening of the second day, the battery level was at 19%. There is no way this watch’s battery could last for 30 days! I really wanted to like this watch because my son gave it to me for Christmas, but I’m feeling more and more that he wasted his money. Don’t waste yours; spend your money on something better. There’s a reason this watch is ranked #7,811 (as of 2/12/20) in smartwatches.
