title: 2.5 stars  Definitely not a security camera, but it is a great camera. APP bait and switch.
text:
*****Update 6/12/2021 I have dropped the rating to 3 stars. More like 2.5 now. The cameras still work fine, nothing has really changed with the camera portion of this system. What has changed is the BLINK APP. Previously you would pop your local storage storage in and through the app you would view your videos no problem.

Now Amazon is really trying to push the cloud storage subscription. Upon entering the app you are met with the same camera screen as usual, when you go to the video portion you are now met with a cloud and local storage tabs, instead of one list of videos. This made me a little mad because Amazon decided WITHOUT my permission to move ALL of my videos that were on my local storage to the cloud with no way to move them back to the USB. I could download to my phone or share it via email or messaging app, but I want it on my local storage where I originally chose to put it. Back to the bad about the new tabs for cloud and local storage.

Cons:

1. Slow to bring up list of videos for local storage, but not for the cloud subscription. This was not the case before the app update. I feel this was slowed down intentionally to push people to buy their subscription.

2. Slow to load videos from local storage. This was not the case before the app update. I feel this was slowed down intentionally to push people to buy their subscription. Cloud videos somehow load instantly and local storage you get a message saying "We are retrieving your clip. Hang tight, USB clips take a little longer to load". Local clips played instantly before the update, why all of a sudden do they not? Also the tab no longer highlights your unwatched clips. Not sure if it does this for the cloud subscription.

3. No way to delete multiple clips from local storage. You have to click the video wait for it to load and then click the trashcan in the corner. For the cloud clips you long press on one clip and then you can select multiple clips to delete. Again this was done intentionally to push the cloud subscription over the local storage.

4. You can no longer save live view clips without have a subscription. Before you could select to automatically save your live view with out needing any subscription.

I feel the changes made to the app were a bit extreme. This was supposed to be a product that was easy to use WITHOUT having to subscribe to a cloud service. Now it seems like everything within the app is working against you if you don't have the cloud service. I have had this system since December and I loved it, until the new APP update. I think I might start looking into a different system if things do not change. I fully intend on NOT subscribing to the cloud service.

These are all my opinions and in no way meant to be your deciding factor into what you buy, take this with a grain of salt and do your research to pick what system is best for you.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Overall I am satisfied with my purchase of this system. I bought the 5 camera pack. It works for what my family needs. I did not want to pay almost twice as much for ring cameras to have the real time live view, and then pay extra to have spare rechargeable batteries for when the ones in the cameras died. Also having local storage was a HUGE upside, no fees to pay yearly. If you want a system that alerts you when there is motion and something you can peek at every now and then to see what is going on and have local storage then this is a good system. if you want something that records every second of the day then that you monitor constantly then this is not the system for you. There is always a negative to every system. Do your research and choose what is best for you. the system has been installed for about a week now. I will update when and if needed.

Pros:

Easy setup and configuring.
Local storage (no need for subscription storage) I have a 64gb thumb drive in mine.
You can run power to them if you don't want to depend on batteries. Only downside is once you open the rubber gasket to do this they are not weather proof, but they make cases that will fix that issue.

Cons:

Delay when viewing live view. Real time live view would be nice. I have about a 6 second delay in my "live" view.

title: Good value for a TV!
text:
Originally I purchased the 720p version of this TV sold here, because my old 10+ year 720p store brand TV I bought from Best Buy so long ago finally gave out. I actually really liked that TV and it worked well for a desktop PC that I rarely use. I figured I didn't need to splurge for the 1080p version of this TV since the smaller resolution was perfectly fine for the few times I use my desktop PC. Unfortunately I realized when I hooked up the 720p version, the PC's resolution was actually 1080p, and it was showing through a 720p monitor... long story short, it looked very bad and I realized I had to return it and splurge for the 1080p option. Quick review of the 720p one: Great quality overall, I actually really liked the viewing angles and picture quality of that. I think it would make for a great TV, however for a PC it made the text a bit choppy and difficult to read, so I don't recommend it as that. The same day, I went and ordered this 1080p version. It is designed slightly differently but overall looks the same. Resolution is much better, makes everything on my PC look normal again. I am pretty disappointed with the viewing angles and brightness. The TV is almost darker around the edges. It almost looks like it fades into the edges, which is very strange. Viewing angles are atrocious, but part of that could be attributed to the strange darkness around the edges. Screen is pretty bright, in general for a budget TV I'm happy. But oddly enough the screen on my very old TV that I was using before almost seemed better. Let's just hope I get another 10+ years use out of this one!

The setup was very, very easy. It tries to make you register for a Roku account however look carefully at all your options, you can choose to ignore the setup (it was completely unnecessary for me) and go straight to using it as a computer monitor. The setup however is pretty easy and self explanatory. The "smart" aspect of this TV works well, it's not laggy at all like other smart TVs I have (though they are older as well). I would totally suggest getting this if you plan on using it as an actual TV. As a PC monitor it's alright, but I can't help but feel like since you're looking at it closer up when as a PC monitor, it might be better to spend a little more for a better brand with a better quality panel. This here gets the job done but I'm not wowed. Another pro is that it is VERY, very light. I was shocked at how light it was. Definitely not what I'm used to from my older flat screen TVs!

title: Outstanding gear
text:
Right up front, I am a network engineer for a wireless broadband provider, so take that into account as you read my comments.

I have an e410 AP in the wall between my kitchen, diningroom, and livingroom. I have an e430w on the wall at the end of the hallway between bedrooms. And I have an e700 outside behind the carport. (this review will be copied/pasted for all three devices) I did NOT purchase them from Amazon, I received them directly from Cambium over the past few years. (We use Cambium brand equipment for our wireless broadband network, they were sent to me as a "thank you" for active & helpful web forum participation)

The e430w is surprisingly capable and flexible, allowing a wide variety of hookups, including running the AP via POE (PowerOverEthernet) and then re-feeding POE out on another port. (to power a camera, as I do from my e700, or a VOIP desk phone, as I do from my e430w) There's actually four gigabit ports on the e430w, the ether1 port (POE input to power the AP) is on the back, so in an ordinary installation it would be inside the wall box. So too is a 'passthrough' port that is directly wired to another 'passthrough' port on the bottom of the unit beside the 3 'external' gigabit ports. this port is handy if you need to power it via POE but locally, or if you have an older phone system jack in the wall that you want to replace with the e430w while providing passthrough for the existing phone.

The e700 is outside, close to the middle of my 3 acre property, and provides me workable wifi throughout the back 2/3 of the property and along the driveway. (other parts of the front are blocked by the house itself) There are surely places where coverage is spotty, but I have about 2 acres of woods back there...

The e410 in my kitchen is, by comparison, mundane. It works reliably, there's typically 8-15 devices connected to it.

These APs are intended to be centrally controlled, either by the cloud-hosted (and free) cnMaestro service (cloud.cambiumnetworks.com) or by a local cnmaestro-on-premises, but (unlike, for example, Ubiquiti wifi) you CAN configure these radios manually directly logged into them via web browser. You can also (NOT tried this, myself) designate one of multiple APs sharing a local network as the controller, and any settings you change there (like WPA encryption key, for example) will propogate to the other APs.

In short, if you know what you're doing, all three of these APs are outstanding products, and well supported. If you DON'T know what you're doing, you might puzzle through it (again, unlike Ubiquiti these can be configured by had) but I'd suggest enlisting the assistance of someone with some wireless networking experience. In any case, these guys are solid performers, well worth the price if you need to support more devices, more complex setups, etc. (I have 4 SSIDs active on mine sometimes, locked into isolated independant VLANs, one forced through a click-through-portal since it's unsecured)

title: Just buy a Sandisk
text:
I bought this micro SD card with a Vantrue N4 dash cam because the description recommends this one and said not to use a sandisk or transcend card. I ended up having to purchase two of these cards because the first one was lost in shipping. When one did come, it failed to format in the dash cam and a computer wouldn’t even recognize the card. After attempting to format it in the dash cam, I took the card out and it was ridiculously hot for being used for only about 30 seconds. I also tried plugging the dash cam into a wall outlet with the card in it and it would glitch out and turn on and off repeatedly in 2-3 second intervals. It would record in black & white, flip the camera, the screen would blink rapidly, etc.

I contacted customer service about all of these issues and left my number for a phone call that was promised within 24 hours. They never called, one person emailed me later and told me that I needed to update my dash cam to format my micro SD card. However the only way to actually update your dash cam is to do so with a micro SD card that is ALREADY formatted and working properly. Plus my dash cam’s firmware did not need to be updated as it was brand new. Customer service had no response for the lost card and hasn’t issued a refund for either one yet.

I returned this card and purchased a sandisk ultra card for much cheaper at target. I found that sandisk resolved their micro SD card issues in dash cams over 2 years ago. As long as you buy a newer one that has “A1” stamped on it. It works flawlessly, I can view and save the videos on my computer or dash cam and none of the previous problems have occurred since.

title: It Will Satisfy a Hardcore Cord Cutter
text:
For those who want a true Android TV box, that runs Android TV OS and is certified to run apps like Netflix and Prime Video in HD/4K, buy an NVidia Shield. It's pretty much the only choice. I have one, and love it. On the other hand, if you're the type of person who laughs at the idea of using either of those two apps, and gets their content elsewhere - OR, already has a Shield, and just wants another box: this is a great choice. For those users, you'll first need to put aside Antutu and Geekbench scores. In real world usage, this box performs VERY respectably. There are a few things you'll want to know, or already suspect:
The standard remote is awful. The bundled mini keyboard remote is fine, but only if you don't use any other similar remote regularly for another device. On this one, the volume and direction navigation pads are reversed from any other similar looking mini keyboard I've ever used. You'll never get used to it, so just use another more standard mini keyboard (if you read this far, you've already got spares laying around). My version of this box does have Bluetooth capability, despite what I saw in Chigz YouTube review, so that's an added plus for remote options. Now, you'll also be wanting to install another launcher. In the photo I attached, you'll see I'm using ATV Launcher. Also: for some reason, the audio output is a bit low. There's no reason you can't just bump up the TV or audio system volume, but if you want to have it as it really should be (compared to other attached devices you might have), consider installing Volume Booster by GOODEV (it's in the Play Store). A 15% boost is all it needs.
So, on to all the good stuff:
Despite performance scores on paper, this box runs really well. No frustrating UI lags, and most importantly, it's _odi and IPTV friendly. Even a heavy _odi build like the Xanax build runs well. And, for some reason, this box actually seems a bit more _odi friendly than even the Shield. Also, unlike some other lower priced Android boxes I've tried, the _odi UI runs at 1920x1080p at 60hz. Video can and does display in full 4K, but it's nice to have the interface itself in 1920x1080, instead of maxing out at 720, as it does on some other boxes. Playing content from a media server on my home network, and streaming from places unknown, has been great. As long as the server can deliver, and you've got the internet speed, 4K videos play without buffering or frame drops. Having said that, the ethernet connection is max'd out at 100Mbps on this box, but that's not an issue for me, as everything works well with the 75Mbps down I've got, and running IPVanish.
I could probably ramble on, but suffice it to say, that no Android box is perfect, but this one is truly a solid performer at this price.
I have received no compensation, financial or otherwise, from anyone. I bought this with my own money, and I'm not once of the thousands of shills on here. 😃

title: Great system for the price that with a few tweaks can be better.  I'll explain.
text:
Buying a pre-built makes a lot of sense in the current market due to scalping prices of current video cards so I decided to give this pre-built by MSI a shot. I'm very glad I did! It's a wonderful system that can be made even better with a little work and a tweak here and there. Here's what your getting into and here's how to make the best out of it. First, the shipping was good and the packaging was very well done to ensure nothing was broken.

I was worried the parts that can be random would be lower tier but they are actually pretty solid. The nvme was Crucial Brand at 2kmbps. The ram was Gaming Dio at 3k mhz. The video card is the Ventus OC version. It's running newer games in 1080p gloriously with a couple of them with ray tracing enabled (the ones currently available anyways) without a hitch. My version was supposed to be the 10700kf but it came with the 10700k instead which is a nice little addition but not that big of a deal considering it's a system designed for gaming so you obviously will be using a standalone video card but the internal is nice to have for backup and testing purposes.

If your going for 1080p max settings with smooth frames for current and near future generation games the version with the 2070 super is perfect for that. Now being a pc gamer for many years I know my way around a pc so here's why it's only a 4 star rating instead of 5 and what you can do to fix it.

First, the aio liquid cooled rad is in a bad location and needs to be moved to the top of the case instead of being used as the back exhaust. This will ensure better flow and make sure any air bubbles or air in the aio will be at the top of the radiator and not hanging around the cpu. This made about a 4-5c difference on cpu temps as well and will help expand the lifespan of the aio. The way they had it looped around to the back exhaust location was just bad flow. You don't have to take it off the cpu and repaste it or anything just unscrew the fan/rad and move it to the top of the case and screw it in there. By doing this you are going to want a new back exhaust so I would make sure to order an extra case fan when you purchase the system so they both arrive at the same time. I ordered a coolermaster argb fan and it worked perfect and connected right to the motherboard fan slot near the back of the case (where they had the aio connected to) and even had room on the rgb contoller to hook that up as well. Speaking of which.....

Since they had the aio mounted to the back they had the power wire connected to the rear case exhaust slot on the motherboard when if you look closely at the motherboard there is clearly a pump labeled slot once you move the aio rad to the top make sure to plug the power into the power slot labeled "pump" on the top right of the motherboard which was designed for that very reason which had nothing plugged into it. This will ensure it reads right in the bios and in your software like the dragon center and hwmonitor and it ramps up the fan accordingly.

Second, they didn't have the rgb to the cpu cooler connected to the rgb controller. The fan on the radiator had lights and was working but not the MSI dragon on the cpu itself. Taking off the backside of the case revealed it was still wrapped up in a tie just hanging there and simply just had to be plugged in to the empty slot on the controller.

Lastly the windows 10 version and the dragon center software it came with was pretty bad and wonky and windows 10 updates were locking up with issues and it just felt a little bloated. I really recommend crashing the hard drive and reformatting with your own fresh copy of windows 10. They had my single nvme drive split up into 3 different partitions which was just unnecessary. Remove all the partitions and install a fresh windows 10 from a usb drive will make everything much cleaner and smoother. REMINDER: Make sure if you don't have any other computers around to download your wifi drivers for whatever wifi card they put into your system before reformatting your drive or you will not have the internet and won't be able to set it up properly. Once you get your wifi/internet driver the rest can be done after the formatting long as you can connect to the internet. Download the newest version of dragon center and it will be able to find all your other drivers and software and get things running super smooth.

Otherwise it really is a wonderful system and MSI did very well with the part selection in it. I would recommend no problem long as you are a little computer savy and know how to fix the issues I laid out above. I am ready for Night City! Cyberpunk here I come!

As an after thought and not specifically a problem related to MSI or the build. The RTX cards are pretty beefy cards and have a bit of weight so I would recommend something to help hold them up to prevent video card sag and from breaking your pcie slot in the future. My Samus Amiibo worked perfect for that and at the correct height. This will help keep the card straight in the slot and not weighted down and saggy which could cause issues in the future. Happy gaming everyone!

THIS sub sounds muffled and sounds like a lot of wind being blown at high speed into you floor. Kind of like a quick burst from a high speed vacuum.

It still does the job, thats why I gave it 3 stars but there are better subs like Klipsch or BIC america for the same amount. Also go with the front firing subs, this one is down-firing, not as clean an experience if you ask me.

Also you dont have to timbre-match your speakers with your sub, meaning they can be from any make or model...

title: Decent camera for a decent price
text:
In the past I purchased the first gen of the stick up cam for my driveway. Due to too much interference even with a WiFi extender, I ended up returning that camera. Now, due to someone or something in my backyard at 2am that my dog alerted me to, I decided to try this third gen. My back porch is much closer to the router so I was hoping it wouldn’t have issues.

Let’s start off with what can be improved. Previous Ring items I purchased included the drill bits necessary to mount into brick and concrete. This does not. However, the nails and anchors to fit into the drill bit I used for the ring doorbell. But if you don’t have one of those, you would be out of luck and need to purchase a masonry drill bit set. As for the motion sensor zones, there are three fields of detection that you can turn on or off. I just wish the range went further. What would be even better is if the motion sensor detection could be customized just like the front Ring doorbell. Furthermore, wifi connection is just okay. Though I did expect better since the router was just 15-20 feet away from the camera. However, even when the signal was considered weak, the camera did happen to still go to live view quickly and capture and notify me walking out onto the porch. Lastly, the battery does take a long time to charge. About 4-6 hours. I do recommend getting a second battery so you have one on hand when one gets low. When the system first started up I got a notification that battery was low. I thought it was odd but it then it corrected itself and is at 100% charge.

Now, on to the good stuff. Overall, I’m fairly impressed. This third gen has sturdier parts. First gen had a flimsy mount and face plate that could easily crack. This has a sturdy rubberized plate you mount to and the rest of the camera easily slides onto that. Set up was much faster than expected. Just a quick press of a button and scan of the QR code and it was done! You do have to wait about 5 minutes for the camera to do an internal update. I wish we could still post pictures with our reviews. The image quality is crystal clear. Day and night time. Even better than that of my Ring doorbell pro. Finally, I do love that they kept the feature that you can set off a siren from your phone. It’s not obnoxiously loud but loud enough to grab someone’s attention or scare off some crooks.

title: This laptop is a solid alternative for creative artists.
text:
the Asus MB16AC monitor is not compatible with this laptop out of the box.

model UX534FT-DB77 does not support display port over usb.

also this laptop display ads. i mean, asus ads and pop ups on screen. not acceptable for this price range.

UPDATE 9/11/2020

How do I use this laptop?

• Photoshop
• Illustrator
• DaVinci Resolve
• Premiere Pro
• Adobe Dimension
• Other Adobe creative apps.

This laptop is slowly growing in me. I often work with two apps open at the same time, like Illustrator and Photoshop or Dimension and Photoshop, and I am happy to report this laptop can handle large high-resolution images with both apps open without breaking a sweat.

Stays fast and snappy under heavy load and that is a must for my line of work.

Rendering time for Premiere Pro and Resolve are decent enough considering is a laptop. 4K short clips for 30 seconds YouTube ads render in minutes. Not bad.

The small touchpad/monitor is unusable for most applications but has a few nice tricks that can be useful for creative work. For example, when working on Words or Excel it can automatically display a shortcut window that is quite useful, and you can configure the tiny screen to display custom shortcuts for selected apps like Photoshop and Illustrator so your most common shortcuts are right there whenever you need them. File Explorer, Spotify and Chrome are unusable on the small screen because the text is too small to be readable. When the small screen is in touchpad mode it behaves like any other touchpad. Nothing odd to report here. Anyways, I do recommend using a mouse even when out of home or the office.

The laptop build is beautiful and feels sublimely premium to the touch. Battery is nowhere close to expectations, at least, not for my applications. If you are an artist be aware battery time can cut down to six hours (even less if rendering) under heavy load, so get a spare charger if you plan to use it on the go. I guess a student may squeeze more battery time if they are not tempted to gaming when on History class, but I am not a student, so I am just taking a guess. The screen is glossy and very prone to reflections but will display a sharper and clearer image artist will appreciate. Keyboard is very standard, no praises and no complains. Its comfortable and will do what you expect from a keyboard. Must mention, the keyboard has a few of function-shortcuts that can be useful. For example, there is a calculator shortcut and a shortcut to change the modes for the small touchpad screen.
Graphic card is decent enough for 3D applications. If you create 3D assets on Photoshop, After Effects or Dimension (I have not tested other apps) then I am happy to report this laptop will handle your needs. I tried a few games with good results. The Witcher 3 and Portal 2will run smoothly with medium settings.

WHAT I DO NOT LIKE?

Honestly, at this price point Alt Mode Display Port should be a standard feature. But no, that is reserved for the top-dollar models when it comes to Asus. That means I can not use any of my portable Alt Mode monitors when I’m doing a presentation to my clients on my local Chili’s or when I have to demo a marketing campaign to a board full of tie and suit wearing guys with a bunch of MacBook’s on a large rectangular table. It just makes me look cheap and for a businessman like me, appearances are important. If I knew about this little flaw, I would had purchased something else instead. I didn’t returned because my previous laptop died and I was in desperate need of a replacement.

VERDICT

This laptop is a solid alternative for creative artists who will mainly use on a desk with occasional on the go trips for short periods of time.

• Razer Basilisk Ultimate HyperSpeed Wireless Gaming Mouse w/ Charging Dock

title: Before you buy, what you need to know
text:
Summary: the Momentum 3s sound great and are well built. Fantastic for music, and good enough for calls.

Sound quality: This is the reason to splurge for the Momentum 3s. Great, full-range, tight bass, clear mids and highs. Make sure you've enabled aptX and the maximum bitrate for AAC (search online for instructions on Mac and Android). If you install the Sennheiser app, you can change equalizer settings, like if you want Beats-level bass boost. After playing around, I decided I like the default sound best.

Video: Sounds great. I've experienced no lag with Netflix, YouTube, or Prime Video.

Comfort: Like all over-ear headphones, these can get a little warm. Fine for me. They're also heavier than the all-plastic Bose 700 and Sony XM3, because the Momentum 3s are built with real metal and leather. Weight is similar to the B&W PX7 and B&O H9. I find it ok, and worth it for the sound quality.

Bluetooth: They pair with 2 devices concurrently for audio, and I have them paired with 3 devices in total (MacBook, iPad, and Android phone). Switching works fine.

Controls: They have physical buttons that you learn to find by touch. I find them more reliable and less finicky than touch gestures. (The H9 touch controls didn't work for me at all.) The setting to auto-mute when you remove from your head just didn't work properly for me though. It would mute and unmute if I nodded my head. I turned off the setting, and don't miss it. Not a big deal. The transparency mode is easy to activate with a switch. Some reviewers complain about how you have to fold them to turn them off. I find it no big deal -- it's easy to see that they're folded and off, vs not being sure if the little red light is on.

Build quality: High quality. Solid. Real metal and leather. Downside: they're a little heavier than all-plastic cans like Bose and Sony. I pinched myself with the metal when unfolding them. I can deal.

Case construction: Nice round case, looks high end. It's soft, not hard. It's small enough for my carry on bag and commuter bag. It includes a pocket for a cable in case your battery runs down. Works for me.

Call quality: Sound is great when other people are speaking. At first, I found them pretty awkward for calls, due to the lack of sidetone (hearing your own voice), and would have recommended them only for occasional calls, not if you make lots of video and phone calls. Then I discovered that the app has a setting to give you sidetone! Turn on Transparency mode, and check the box to play music at the same time. Now you can hear the outside world, including your own voice, so you know you're not shouting. Problem solved!

Noise cancellation: Not the main reason why I bought them. This is a bonus feature for me. It helps with public transit and plane noise, and definitely gets the level down enough to make the music or video sound enjoyable. If your #1 goal is noise cancellation, Bose or Sony is probably what you want.

Design: It's subjective. I like the look better than all but the Bang & Olufsen H9s. The white + brown version of the M3s is stylish, though I went with the black.

Conclusion: After extensively researching the options in this price range, and trying multiple headphones, this is the pair I'm keeping. For my personal preferences, these are a winner.

title: A solid table at a budget price
text:
It's virtually impossible these days to go to an actual brick-and-morter audio store and compare turntables side by side. Even the few dealers who sell them don't have them set up that way. So we're left with what information we can find online. In quick comparisons of this table and others in it's price range (Pro-Ject, Rega) one thing jumps out at you right off - the Ortofon Blue cartridge that comes with this table. As you can see in a lot of the reviews here, it does get your attention.

Putting a $250 cartridge on a $500 turntable is either impressive or silly. Impressive if the turntable as a whole is up to the quality of the cartridge; silly if it's putting high-end racing tires on a Hyundai. Turns out, it's justifiably impressive.

I can't make one of those, "this is the best turntable for the money" claims because I haven't heard all the other tables out there. But I can say that I'm both impressed and surprised to find this level of quality at this price.

Pros
The fit and finish are excellent. Nothing (except maybe the slightly flimsy cueing lever) feels cheap or plastic.

Set-up is a 15 minute breeze, and the included instruction manual is far better than most.

The "auto-stop" feature works (and doesn't seem to be available on most tables of this price.) It's a godsend for those of us who can't jump up out of a chair as quickly as we once could.

Finally and most importantly, the sound is great. Tight, detailed, and it creates a soundstage that only vinyl can - the sense that the musicians are right there in front of you. I've always held that a well-made LP played on a well-made turntable beats digital sound every time. That's a statement that starts lots of arguments, but this turntable is certainly up to the task of proving the point.

Cons
If you tap the plinth while the table is running it creates a pretty hefty boom through your speakers, meaning the plinth is fairly resonant. This probably won't cause most people any real-world problems (you're not going to be tapping the thing while it's playing), but it could cause some loss of resolution if your music is both very loud and very bass heavy. It may also be the reason that the Fluance, even more than most turntables, benefits by having the dust cover removed while playing. (Which is actually quite easy - Fluance has designed the thing to lift straight out without having to flex the hinges.)

There is no way to adjust either the vertical tracking angle (VTA) on the tonearm or the azimuth on the cartridge. I'm sure that won't be a big deal to most people buying a turntable at this price, but it may frustrate those who like to tweak things a lot.

The lack of VTA adjustment and the fairly high mass of the tonearm will limit the choices you have of cartridges you may want to use if you feel like changing things around. The Fluance website offers some guidance in terms of what cartridges will work...but a lot won't. Again, probably not a deal-breaker, given that the Ortofon cartridge it comes with is excellent.

Does not have a stereo mode to link to another device but my Samsung device allows for streaming a single output to two devices.
I compared this to a JBL Charge 3 (unfair) and also a the BVI BOOMERVIVI (decent equivalent) and the takeaway is that this has better sound (no bass heavy) then the JBL but overall is not as loud at the same reproduction quality as the BVI BOOMERVIVI. I mentioned this since if the BVI BOOMERVIVI rolls "face" down the sound changes and that does not happen with the SiverOnyx.
If you are going to want something exclusively for portable or non horizontal then go for the BVI BOOMERVIVI but for a fixed location like on the desk at work the SiverOnyx is a better choice.

title: A little persnickity
text:
I often work from home and want to have a great video conferencing setup. For me this means a green screen with great lighting. Unfortunately, my new employer uses video conferencing software (WebEx) that doesn't natively support chroma key. This posed a challenge, how could I get a chroma key effect, like what Zoom provides, without installing additional software on my work machine? The answer? Use OBS on another machine and create an over the top video conferencing setup.

Here's where things got challenging, although the device worked in any resolution with Google Hangouts and the occasional client Zoom call, WebEx would show the device as being present, but it would just show a gray screen. I tried different resolutions, and once in a while I'd get it to work, but most of the time, it was the gray screen. Finally, in a fit of frustrating, I decided to use a USB-C to USB-A cable and just put the device on the USB2 bus, and now it works fine. I'm not capturing 4k and USB2 provides enough bandwidth for HD Webcams, so this works, but I can't help but feel like the box is a little rough around the edges when it comes to USB-C/USB3.

This was futher shown by how it needed to be directly connected to my MacBook Pro over USB-C, if I attempted to plug it into a USB-C port on my thunderbolt dock it would end up doing something that required me to unplug all USB-C devices before it, or any other USB-C/Thunderbolt 3 devices worked again.

So, does the device work? Yes.

Does it capture 4k? I dunno. I only go up to 1920x1080 right now.

Does it let me do really great stuff with OBS for my video conferences? Yes.

Was it unnecessarily frustrating? Yes.

I have a hunch that this thing will continue to be frustrating. For my HDMI camera input I think I'll just go with Elgato Cam Link instead.

title: Decent alternative to Cotton Carrier
text:
Purchased the Dual Camera version to hold a Sony A7iii and a Sony A6000 with various telescopic lenses up to 300mm (no giant lenses tried like the 100-400GM, etc.). Quality is good, but you have to get your mind around hanging $3,000 off a plastic plate on the vest. Yes the round piece that attaches to the camera is metal, but the vest plate is plastic. The plastic plate is sewn into the vest with reasonable quality, although the stitching is haphazard, one side being crooked by maybe 5-10 degrees in my case. Comparing to Cotton Carrier instructional video, I see a few little things missing with the Nicama, for example: (1) the round camera mounts are directional; on the CC model there is an arrow to guide you which way to locate it when screwing it down, no such indicators on the Nicama; (2) also on camera mounts, CC includes a tripod mounting thread, none on Nicama; (3) side holster appears to be quite a bit bigger on the Nicama; (4) CC retainer clips on the vest are black, while silver on the Nicama which makes them stand out and may cause reflections in the field to scare off critters. None of these are critical, especially when saving $130 for a nice-to-have accessory. But as with all things, if you are concerned with fine details and don't mind spending 5x the price, the CC may be for you.

Update 03/14/2019: two days after receiving the Nicama vest, I stumbled upon a Cotton Carrier vest at a local camera shop. What I thought were minor differences turned out to be significant. In a nutshell, the CC vest is a far better product, so have returned the Nicama. Vest material is padded in key spots, well stitched, buckles are much stronger without being stubborn, adjustments are easier, and it just looks 10x better. The Nicama material has that "sticky plastic" feel while the CC vest feels like high quality. All parts are coated black to minimize reflections in the field. Side holster is smaller and the vest is just a lot more comfortable when dangling two cameras from it. The CC vest has a separate strap across the front to hold down the center camera, nice feature. The CC hubs that attach to the camera are noticeably more robust, and include a 1/4-20 threaded hole so you don't lose the tripod mount. Took it out to the field this morning, for me the extra investment was well worth it. Still 4 stars for the Nicama, as it does work, and its fighter-brand pricing means it should continue to serve many folks well.

title: Major Security Flaw
text:
The system seems to work and generally perform to the specs listed in the description, however, there is a major security flaw that is a deal breaker. The only way to have multiple member of the household access the cameras is to share the account login credentials. This means that everyone has access to view the cameras has FULL ADMINISTRAVTIVE ACCESS. The problems with this are obvious and many, including:

1. My technology-challenged MIL can accidentally start messing with system settings.
2. My pre-teen kids can mess with settings and erase recorded content.
3. My account password is on many devices not under my direct control.

100% unacceptable.

I invite you to peruse the blink forums where many customers have been demanding this fix for years, and tech support just keeps recommending sharing passwords. It's patently absurd that a tech behemoth like Amazon is telling users to share passwords across devices. Password sharing is perhaps the most fundamental violation of basic IT security.

So, if you live alone, this camera system could work for you. If you are looking for a home security system that your whole family can safely use, this ain't it.

I will be returning my system for a refund and finding something that can cross the hurdle of minimum basic system security.

Manufacture of electronic Rotor ( antenna) The minium gauge.. The most important information about purchasing any wire..the gauge, the material used in manfacturing ..ie..copper..steel with copper coating, aluminum, ect.
Wish the gauge I purchased from Amazon supplier was shown in the details of the wire.
The wire gauge for use this product should be suffice for a very light duty rotor,with a small antenna..a short run..less than 25 feet..length of cable from rotor to inside of building with controller box.

title: Review
text:
Having used the laptop sleeve for three months now, I am confident to say that this laptop sleeve has provided me with great functionality, impeccable style, and essential safety at a reasonable price. I bought the CCPK 13-inch laptop sleeve for my 13-inch MacBook Pro from Amazon because as a college student, I need to carry my laptop everywhere and in all kinds of conditions. This sleeve keeps my laptop protected from water and snow, while the synthetic black colored cloth makes it decently modish.

Safety
The sleeve is made out of neoprene; however, it doesn’t feel like it as much. Usually, products made out of synthetic substances are fragile, but this sleeve is very safe. The sponginess of the cloth keeps the laptop protected from any external pressure. When kept in a bag with books and other objects, the cushion outside the cover prevents the laptop from bumping or getting scratches.

Style
There are three different colors that a customer can choose from: black, pink and mint green. I chose black as it matches with my MacBook and is easy to clean if it gets dirty. I have been using this product for three months and I haven’t even cleaned it once, even though it has fallen on dirty floors a couple of times. This is because it is made out of synthetic neoprene which makes it resistant to water and stains.

Functionality
I really think that this product is safe but for additional safety, I had ordered a laptop case to make it completely secure. Even though my laptop is surrounded by a hard-shell cover, the sleeve still provides enough space to keep my laptop. For accessories, I just carry it in my school bag. The zipper did get stuck when I tried to unzip the sleeve once but applying oil to the outer zip fixed the problem easily and I have not had any problems with the zipper since.

Overall, this product is great, as it is one of the cheapest and efficient means to protect my laptop from scratches, dust, and water. I am really satisfied with the product and would recommend this to everyone who is looking forward to buying a cheap and efficient means to protect their laptop, I am glad that I found this product.

title: Great sound quality, Amazing price, Button layout needs some work
text:
Right off the bat, the first thing that I noticed I liked with these IEM’s are the ear hooks: THEY'RE FLEXIBLE! This is such a huge improvement over the hard/stationary ear hooks that’s typical for these cars of ear phones. The soft and flexible nature of the hooks make putting them on much easier, and removing the earphones is quick and doesn’t hurt my ear like the hard ear hooks of other models.

Sound quality is great and on-par with other IEMs. Much of the sound quality and sound isolation comes from making sure you have a snug fit with the silicone tips in your ears. These come with multiple sizes of tips so you shouldn’t have an issue finding the right size.

I love that the wire is the ‘non-tangle’ kind. The smooth and wide shape of the wire really helps against tangling and can be extended to full length very easily. An absolute boon to ear phones that still use a wire.

The one real complaint I have is with the UX layout of the buttons. When you put these ear phones on, the (-) volume button is facing forward and the (+) is facing backwards. In other words, when being worn, the (-) button is essentially ABOVE the (+) button. This may not be an issue for some people, but for me, it’s extremely unintuitive; Because the volume buttons are essentially ‘flipped’ when being worn, I end up raising the volume instead of lowering the volume and vice versa. Considering that in order to Skip and Backtrack songs are controlled via the volume buttons, this also becomes an issue.

One other issue I have is with the main button. Sometimes, it just doesn’t register my input when I want to stop/start my music. After a few tries, it will start registering again.

Overall, for the price, these are really good Bluetooth IEMs. Sounds quality is great along with the noise reduction, and the non-tangle wire is very convenient. The flexible ear hooks are a real nice touch. The only things that really annoyed me were the unintuitive layout of the volume buttons and the occasional fickleness of the pause/play button.

title: Nearing 1080ti performance PLUS Tensor and RT cores for great price
text:
GPU's really just do what they say on the tin. I have an Alienware 13r3 with a GTX 1060 6GB and a 3440x1440 ultra-widescreen LG monitor, and it really chugs in modern games at native monitor resolution. It gets literally too hot to touch, fans sound like jet engines, and many games just aren't fun to play when you've always gotta tweak everything down to a mix of low, med and high options to get the perfect mix of quality visuals and playable frames.

Then I got this Zotac. I was looking for as good a 2070 as I could get at the $500 pricepoint (got it for $520 on amazon, not sure if that's permanent), and the Amp Extremes come with A-designated (aka pre-binned) core, the highest factory overclock on the market, and is absolutely SILENT. I'm using it through an Alienware Graphics Amplifier and holy lord, I went from having about a 1-hour limit (from overheating) on any game, deafening fans, painfully hot laptop, and mid-range internal GPU that even fully cooled only pulled medium options for any modern game. Now I crank up even the worst culprits (Car Mechanic Sim 2018, Battlefield 1, RB6:Siege) and not only can I crank it up to ultra, but I can even do crazy stuff that normally topped out the 6GB in the 1060 like using ultra-high-res textures that take 6-7GB of VRAM. The laptop is cool to the touch, the Zotac is almost silent even after hours of gaming, and I'm future-proofed with DLSS, Tensor, and RT capabilities for future titles. Plus performance that outdoes RTX 1080's easily. If you've got $500 to spend and have a GTX 1060 or below, at this price point, this is the best option on the market.

title: Great deal for $79 - Works as described
text:
For the original $349 price, this 3rd party cable box is not too attractive (TiVo does so much more). But as a $79 solution to scrambled digital cable, it's a steal!

I installed this box on Spectrum in Los Angeles with a CableCard and TuningAdaptor. Spectrum sent a tech for free and it took him well over an hour to authorize these devices to my account, but once he did, this device does pretty-much what it says: It gets every cable channel, but with no recording ability. Also, there are no "legacy" (analog) outputs -just HDMI and an optical audio jack.

I've heard that Samsung support is dying (or dead) so I wasn't really expecting a program guide, but to my surprise, the guide does work!

The box also has built-in WiFi, apps for streaming services, and the ability to play video from a hard disk or memory stick. I haven't tested these features.

Spectrum charges about $10/month for a cable box plus $8-$12 for DVR service (which this box DOES NOT have), but they only charge $2.20/month for the CableCard (TuningAdaptor included), so as you can see, this device will save you more money than LED lightbulbs!

title: Great sound but do not stay in my ears
text:
So since the virus lockdown I have been on a quest for the perfect wireless buds that will stay in when I work out (and I work out hard!). I used to do jiu jitsu (no headphones allowed!) but with the virus I have taken up circuit training and elliptical and running, and the buds I was using (jabra 65t) were fine for hanging out but not vigorous work outs. The Jabras kept falling out. I do have a deformity in my right ear from wrestling so nothing works as well in that ear, but even the left Jabra bud would fall out when I ran. Otherwise they are very good buds.

So then I bought the Jaybird Vistas The Jaybirds come with a wing tip that I thought would solve my problem. So here are the pluses. Excellent sound and base (better than Jabra)! Rapid and reliable paring. Excellent case with good size, feel and function. Class 7 water proof. Excellent companion app that controls EQ and also button function (super useful) These buds are sturdy, light and function extremely well. Here are the down sides. When they are in place they really seal the ear canal so that every step is an internal thud in your head. With sweat the seal is even more annoying. Because of this when someone talks to me I want to take the bud out and it does not have a proximity sensor so it does not automatically stop. I have to take the extra step of pushing the pause button. Not a deal breaker at all, just saying. But I still could not get the right bud to stay in when I work out. The left was always fine but these are proprietary wing tips that function as one unit and only come in small medium and large. They do not allow separate adjusting of the bud portion versus the wing tip (which can be found in other devices such as the much much cheaper but very good wired anker soundcore spirits). The rubber is also thick and not as comfortable as other tips. So if you have weird asymmetric ears these may be a problem for you. If you want some ambient noise or venting in your ear canal these may not be right for you. But if you have normal symmetric ears and have never had a problem with ear bud fit these are awesome buds.

Note: I returned the Jaybirds and have since tried the Powerbeats Pro as well as the Master and Dynamic Go buds. Both of these have crisper all around sound than the Jaybirds but maybe less powered base.
The Master and Dynamic Go buds have excellent battery life, a good case, good connection and very nice sound (crisp in all ranges, but not for heavy base lovers). They don't have a companion app or proximity sensor and the buttons are also a little small to easily find during exercise. The buttons are also a little small to easily find during exercise. Unfortunately their take on wing tips to maintain fit sucks. They just don't stay in when I work out, even my good left ear. They came up with a proprietary wing that seems like a good idea and is separately sized than the tips (so you can do a lot of mixing and matching), but they just don't work that well compared to normal wings (which Bose has been doing for years). They are very comfortable though and if you have very normal ears these might be the buds for you. I wanted to keep these but they just didn't do what I needed them to do.

The Power beats pro are the best. They have excellent sound which is extremely crisp (though the tip size needs to be experimented until they create a good seal-this is important). The base is not overwhelming and the sound is as good as the Master and Dynamic buds (which are famed for their sound). They are vented so that sound filters in and I don't have that trapped in my own head feel. The buttons are identical on both sides and easy to use. I am an android user and they still work and pair extremely well including with voice activated google assistant (versus Siri). Most importantly they completely solve FOBFO (fear of buds falling out). Its like being an insomniac for all of your life and taking an ambien for the first time! They do not budge no matter what exercise I do. They have a hook that slides around the whole ear so they are more obtrusive and are quite visible. They are also not the most comfortable (the master and dynamics won that). Down sides: They have a lousy companion app that does not enable fine tuning of equalizer settings and the case is ginormous! There is no way I am carrying that thing around in my pocket. Purse or backpack yes, but not pocket. Fortunately they have 9 hour battery life so I never take the case with me.
Winner: PowerBeatsPro---got them refurbed at Best Buy for $149 and saw them on Amazon for $200 during sale-so don't spend the $249 they are currently advertised for.

title: Lasted 7 Months, Don't Bother Buying
text:
Off the bat, the unit never wanted to connect to my cable modem. I went through the usual steps of rebooting the modem and the WiFi unit, rechecking settings, but always getting the error message that there is something wrong with my internet connection. Should have sent it right back then, but the other ASUS I purchased and returned to a local retailer said that there is a specific sequence to be followed and some older cable modems had issues. Yes, my cable modem was more than 10 years old, but the past 3 or so WiFi routers including an ASUS AC52U connected just fine and worked well for several years.

I gave this latest purchased modem the benefit of the doubt. Since a cable modem replacement was in my near future I made a work around. I connected my old Linksys to the modem and fed the ASUS from one of it's router outputs for around four months. It worked just fine, but I also noticed intermittent "Disconnected" error messages. Yes, it could have been the the Linksys. But after the cable modem was replaced, I removed the Linksys router, and the intermittent "Disconnected" error messages continued to happen. In response to these message I would do a reboot of both the router and the cable modem. But then all of a sudden this third week of January 2020 the "Not connected" error message would not respond to a reboot and was now also displaying a "There is something wrong with the Internet connection". I thought the new cable modem might be failing, but putting my Linksys back on the cable modem, everything was just fine.

The other weird thing is that even though the ASUS complained of being disconnected from the internet, the status of the internet connection showed an active IP address lease. Also, I noticed that while going back and for checking settings and the status, that I would see it briefly show that it was successfully connected and then it would change its status back to "Disconnected".

I searched the web and found a whole community of ASUS users complaining of the same weird problem, it says it's disconnected, but it shows a status of looking like it is connected. All said customer service was of no help which was not encouraging. Some people found a strange fix. They claimed that if you changed the DNS settings by adding them in manually with server addresses of other than your ISP's DNS servers, that that would do the trick and you were magically connected again to the internet. In fact it was claimed that after you did this, and you went back in and changed the DNS setting back to automatic (back to ISP DNS) that it would continue to stay connected. Needless to say, I did this and not only did it not work, but the web interface started locking up and acting erratic. It began kicking me out multiple times trying to log in after I had done any changes to the settings and doing a reboot.

My conclusion is that the configuration has become corrupted, which it is probably why I'm having these issues in the first place. I do not hold out any hope that restoring the configuration will help because it will likely happen again and again. I would guess that it would be due to hardware components failing which would take this to yet another level.

It simply appears that the manufacturer has component and possibly design problems. The bottom line is that it is not worth the aggravation to continue to try and troubleshoot this.. I will not buy any ASUS Wifi routers any more.

title: Great contender for best gaming laptop of 2019
text:
I was trying to decide between this, the Asus Zephyrus M, and the new Razer Blade 15 Advance. After going back and forth, I decided to try out the MSI GS65 and I think this trial phase is on its way to being permanent.

I am a long time Mac user and my current laptop is a MacBook Pro 13 2018 and I game on a PS4 and an Xbox One X. Wanted to get back to the PC Master Race and I wanted the flexibility to play at home, in between offices while I'm on the road as well as have a great dedicated PC that will run my Windows applications for work. I've been using Parallels for years, while it does work... it's just not the same.

Out of the box, the GS65 has decent build quality with its aluminum casing compared to most PC laptops you see at Best Buy but this is nowhere near the level of quality of a Mac and even a Razer. The GS65 doesn't feel as solid and I would have expected a little more after shelling out $2000 for this thing. I really appreciate the engineering of the Mac and Razer on how they were able to build something so thin, yet extremely solid. The build of the MSI screen was disappointingly flimsy and I feel that I could one day break this thing if I opened the screen the wrong way, especially with one hand.

Performance however is where this laptop really shines. I have thrown every game I had at High to Ultra settings and it handles them with ease. Crysis 3 (yeah it's a 2013 game) was at Ultra and it looked amazing. Overwatch was at Ultra and the frame rates just flew and the same with Apex Legends. The GS65 also handled Shadow of Tombraider like a champ. I played through Tombraider on the Xbox One X and I had to sacrifice frame rates for quality and that just wasn't the experience I wanted for such a visually stunning game. On the GS65, Tombraider was absolutely beautiful and it easily maintained a 60 fps frame rate without issues. Sure the fans were blowing but that is to be expected from a thin and light gaming laptop. Oh did I mention that this thing is only a little over 4lbs?

Other things to note:
- The speakers were loud but base is weak.
- Battery life at Battery Saver or Better Battery setting will get you through 4-6 hours for work applications such as MS Office
- The trackpad is much better than last years, but it's no MacBook or Razer
- This has a generous amount of ports, USB 3.0, HDMI, Audio, Mini Display, Thunderbolt
- Wish it had one more thunderbolt port instead of that mini display port
- NO USB-C Charging
- Inverted motherboard makes upgrading a pain, seriously MSI what were you thinking?
- keyboard is a breath of fresh air coming from the stupid butterfly switches of the Mac.
- 240hz screen is fantastic

Overall I think this is a better buy dollar for dollar if you want to compare similar specs to the Razer, you save about $400-$500. title: RAM works great on Mac mini Late 2012!
text:
I recently purchased a Mac mini Late 2012 and I wanted to upgrade the memory on it. I already had 8 GB of RAM from an older computer and wanted to max it out. It's a super easy process. Just twist off the bottom cover, remove the existing RAM sticks, and pop these bad boys right in!

I did find something interesting about this RAM. After you install the memory, you can confirm the memory has been successfully installed by going into System Report. The part number comes up as 484D54343147533641465238412D50422020, which is you convert from ASCII to Hex, it's actually a Hynix HMT41GS6AFR8A-PB. This is legit memory from SK Hynix. SK Hynix memory is actually pretty popular and used by major manufacturers like Dell, Lenovo, and HP. There's absolutely nothing to worry about with this RAM. My Mac mini now runs great (I also installed an SSD).

For anyone that's worried about the RAM being sold under this odd brand name, there's nothing to be worried about. It works great, and I have not had a single issue.

title: Poorly Executed
text:
I was tempted to give the item "2 stars" because it is really disappointing for a Celestron product. But "2 stars" seems at bit harsh.

Harsh or not, "buyer beware." The price, for a "night vision device" is good. But the execution makes me wonder if it would be better to save more now to spend more later to get more. Let's start with what's good....

Construction is quite nice; solid. I like the tripod mount capability (in fact, I would argue using a tripod is essential; more on this in a bit). The scope comes with an 8GB micro-SD card, a front lens rubber cover, a USB charging cable, a video cable, a quick start guide, and a nice storage bag. Even though the box (and quick start guide) say an AC plug doesn't come in the box, there was one in mine. Not at all heavy, either. If you have (or have used) a video handycam you'll feel quite at home with the form factor. But this is where the "good" ends.

In no particular order, here are my concerns/dislikes. First, the aforementioned front lens cover will be easily lost. Unlike a video handycam where the lens cover is "strapped" to the unit this cover once removed has to be put in one's pocket. There is a bit of a lip on the cover so I might be able to jury-rig a strap so that I get what I have on my handycams.

Eye relief is simply awful (especially, if you need to wear glasses). I'm going to have to get used to using this without glasses (which adds a level of inconvenience). The picture also "jiggles" quite a bit in the hand (which is why I think this is best used with a tripod).

The controls (4 buttons on the top of the unit) are not terribly difficult to use, but that's not to say they're easy to use. One really needs to use this unit frequently to get a feel for the button locations and button touch or, if not frequently, very intentionally. Cycling through the menu to adjust settings (such as IR level, screen brightness, zoom, date, mode) is a real pain; just plain clunky. This unit begs to have a similar set-up as a handy cam: a flip-out screen (or something along those lines) to handle, at a minimum, the functions menu.

The complete user manual must be downloaded. It isn't actually all that good. Yes, you'll know what to do and what the unit does, but it could have been better. For instance, you charge the item by opening up the rubber cover on the side of the unit and plug in the USB cable. A red LED comes on. The manual tells the user to charge at least 10 hours before first use. Okay, done. But after close to 15 hours the red light was still on. I would have thought the light would either go out or change color (to green, for example). But it doesn't. Annoying. Also, the manual says to insert the battery cathode (i.e., positive) side first. But that's incorrect. The negative (anode) side needs to go in first; the positive side needs to face forward. Perhaps the writers confused "cathode" and "anode"? And why not just say "positive" or "negative"? Btw, the date/time settings do not reset if you have to remove the battery for a minute or two.

Yes, this unit works; it does what it's advertised to do. But that's only half of the story. The downside is that it just isn't fun using it. So get it if you need it, but I'm guessing you'll be looking for something better pretty quickly.

3 stars.

text:
I bought this system as a replacement for the Cyber Acoustics CA-3602a 62W speakers (https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0027VT6V4), I bought 5 years ago. It spontaneously shorted out while turned off. Talk about planned obsolescence. I honestly would have not purchased from the same company again, but I couldn’t find anything in this price range with the features I needed because of my limited desktop space.

The speakers though more powerful, have the same minimal footprint. There are fewer plugs into the subwoofer so I’m hoping to avoid a shortage this time. The biggest disappointment is the subwoofer. It doesn’t put out nearly as much thumping bass as my old CA-3602a. But it also doesn’t start to distort as quickly either. I bought this in the hopes that the increased wattage would give me better bass, not more muted bass.

It doesn’t sound bad. In fact, it’s quite good room filling sound. It’s just a step down bass wise from my old system. So if you’re not bass hungry and need something that won’t take up too much real estate on your desk, I will still recommend it. But if you’re looking for something that thumps, look elsewhere.

title: For $8.00 A Radio, You Can't Go Wrong!
text: I ordered these as I've grown tired of the nonsense that has flooded the market when it comes to the FRS/GMRS pre-programmed handhelds out there.  As someone who is licensed for the GMRS frequencies, I decided to try these out exclusively on the GMRS frequencies.  Each radio comes with 16 channels (selectable), a small stock antenna, an earpiece with built-in mic, a belt clip, a wrist-wrap and a battery.  First off - DO NOT USE THE RADIOS UNTIL AFTER YOU'VE PROGRAMMED THEM!  with the pre-programmed frequencies, you may interfere with local law enforcement or other off-limits frequencies!  Yes, you have to find the GMRS frequencies.  REMEMBER: These radios are set to 5 watts TX power.  If you are not licensed for GMRS, buy the name brands - as they will be pre-programmed for FRS frequencies and you may use those.  The hardest part is finding the software to program the radios.  I won't paste a link here to where I received the download so as not to upset either Amazon or the website owner.  However, It is searchable on the Internet.  You will need the programming cable so make sure you purchase that.  Once you have the frequencies you want, you can copy and paste them into the software.  Save the file then upload it to the radio.  I did it several times to make a few tweaks to the radio's settings as well as to upload the frequencies I wanted.  Once completed, I did some minor testing at home and the audio was crisp, clear and loud.  I took them with me camping and had my daughter use one while I used another.  She did a little bit of hiking (within a mile of my location) and there were no drop-offs, static on the transmissions or inaudible transmissions (besides those of user error).  The battery life is amazing!  We used them with the power turned on the whole time we were camping (2 full days) and although the battery came close to dying, we were still using full power without drop-off!  I'm going to perform some more extensive testing on these, like taking them out for longer distances to see just how far they'll reach in a more urban setting.  I'm sure that they will have more limited distance due to structures and hills, but I'd like to try anyway.  The only drawback to the radios I received was that two of them came in with the power/volume know 'tight' to turn which indicates a 'bent' component.  Otherwise, they worked perfectly fine.  REMEMBER: You will need to obtain a GMRS license to use these radios AND you must program them before using them so as not to interfere with local law enforcement!  A GMRS license is easy to obtain.  There are no exams/tests for the license, just a simple purchase.  And, the license is good for you and everyone in your immediate family (spouse/child/parent).

title: DO NOT BUY - Horrible connection issues
text:
Hey there yes you the one reading reviews. I was you at one point for this product. I thought oh the bad reviews are likely just some bad customer service or one-off issues. Well, I am here to let you know I have now have 2 of these sound systems. 1 new, 1 certified replacement, and they are likely going to give me a new one as a third attempt with I do not expect to work any differently. Also, customer support tends to not submit requests although they are saying they have so you have to call in and double-check. Customer support has been such an issue for me during this process I am now working directly with an executive to troubleshoot my issues.

For reference, I am using this soundbar with a Vizio Smartcast TV and have had no issues with other soundbars in the past. I am using primarily HDMI-ARC to connect as it is recommended and the best option.

1st soundbar - System firmware updates are whenever it wants even midshow. Numerous firmware flashing was done to be able to connect the soundbar to the wifi. Switch to use the optical connection, this was worse and turned off more often. Eco mode was off, as advised so when audio plays the soundbar should turn on relatively quick. Typically, it won't even turn on. When this happens you have to unplug the soundbar and hold the power button for 5 seconds. Also, it would randomly turn off during shows and it turned off anytime you paused tv steaming services available through Vizio's TV including Netflix, Hulu, youtube, anything with audio would turn the soundbar off when paused.

2nd soundbar - Vizio would only replace my new soundbar with a certified warranty replacement. This to me is unacceptable, those should be sent to be resold in-store at a lower cost. However, I was stuck with it. Unable to get the Wifi to connect again, I gave up as I did not expect to keep it for very long. Using HDMI-ARC again the same main issues with sound. The soundbar will turn off as it chooses, when the tv is paused, and typically will not turn back on when audio begins playing again. Which again with Eco mode off any audio reaching the device should auto turn on the soundbar to the correct audio input. This does not happen.

title: EXACTLY What We Were Looking For
text:
[[VIDEOID:d8331a67c09ad6c9b4b9937cbabcba3]] We recently upgraded our living room TV and wanted to put our old TV in our bedroom. Trouble is, a big ol' TV sitting in a Victorian style bedroom is pretty much like installing a black hole on your wall - sort of sucks every molecule of the decor into its black rectangle and never lets it back out again. What to do? The obvious solution is to make it disappear.

So we did.

My wife's vanity sits at a slight angle and there was just enough room behind it to fit the TV there. This lift was the most cost effective solution I could find. Yes, as other reviewers have noted the instructions included are in Chinese, German and English. And the English is pure gibberish. But there are videos online and the assembly and mounting is actually quite easy - even for a geezer like me. I complicated the installation because I wanted the TV to match the angle at which the vanity sits so it would be more directly facing the bed, so I cut a couple of wedges at 16 degrees and installed them between the lift and the wall using four inch sheet metal screws rather than the hardware provided. All in all - from unpacking to fully operational - I'd say I invested about four hours of my time in this, and that includes measuring and cutting angled wedges, drilling holes, etc.

And - for a while at least - I am a bona fide hero. My wife absolutely loves it! As the video shows, when not in use the TV is completely hidden behind her vanity. Push a button and up it rises - rather dramatically I must say.

When you get right down to it, this is a pretty simple application. You want your TV to go up, you want it to go down, you want the operation to be stable and safe, and - preferably - you want to be able to do it using a wireless remote. I don't know what the other companies making these things are adding that makes them worth three or more times the price, but I can tell you that this lift seems extremely well constructed - nothing flimsy or cheap about it. It even comes with a wired remote as well as the wireless - I don't know why, but it does. The lift isn't fast - the video shows real time from fully down to fully extended. But who wants fast? There is a little bit of drama in watching your TV rise gracefully from nowhere.

A sturdy, well built product that does exactly what you wanted it to do.
A reasonably easy installation - as long as you're willing to watch a few minutes of video to compensate for instructions that might s well be written in Sanskrit.
An outstanding price/value ratio.
And a wife who now considers you to be a DIY deity.
Who could ask for more?

title: Everything looks great but 2 keys stopped working very quickly and it's not acceptable
text:
3 month update: two keys stopped working very quick after buying the product. It was maybe after 1 month I noticed the problems, but I thought I just wasn't used to mechanical keyboards so I stayed with it. Also I wasn't using it everyday, but after about 3 months now I kept getting the same error where it seems the keyboard had problems from near start.

So my 'y' and 'ctrl' keys don't accept input, I end up having to press them 3 times before they'll take an input, basically needing to mash them repeatedly. It's very annoying especially on the 'ctrl' key. It's basically unusable so I'm turning down to a 1 star.

For people not being used to mechanicals, it did improve my typing accuracy which while I wasn't bad at all previously, the keys being raised and slightly seperated did give me a marginal boost that's hard to live without now. It did give increased finger strain from membrane switch keyboards since those had much much flatter keys.

Nonetheless these specific switches (brown) are nice because you dont' need to fully bottom out, unlike other switche types. On these you can quickly find the actuation point midway, and then you can relatively quickly become familiar with how hard your fingers need to press (which helps improve speed and accuracy just a bit more and makes the typing very light).

However flat keys are easier to type on so if you're typing a lot all day I'd just stick with a membrane keyboard or other such flatter-key device. Though I don't know if companies are making membrane keyboards with some of the nice things I list below that I bought the keyboard for.

1. Steel-top
I hate cheap plastic. This should increase it's longevity&durability. I also love how heavy it feels compared to my old full-plastic keyboard.

2. Typefont of the keys is lovely; seen too many ugly-looking fonts for the keys for rgb mechanical kb.

3. Software lets you pick color for each individual key. Also has various rgb modes/colors you can access directly with the FN key and a few other keys on the keyboard. However I'm very happy that I can use its RGB software to color my keys by category (stuff like tab/caps/space/enter/delete are all dark blue, letters are white except asdf-jkl; are red, numbers are light green, etc. etc. Makes it very easy to recognize keys since 1. this is a new keyboard I need to get used to and 2. I use it in low-light situations.

4. Brightness is good but for my very picky preferences I wish it could go a little higher, but I don't think any rgb keyboards in general go higher.

6. Cable is this wonderfully braided material that feels like a type of strong fabric, such that it feels nice to touch but still seems to give amazing support. Cable has a little groove made for it on the bottom of the keyboard so it has very little risk of bending (since the part where the cable enters the keyboard is within that groove) but your keyboard does not lay on the cable either. It's mostly secure in the groove but I do wish there was a little latch just for that extra firm security.

7. Cable is about 5 feet long so it's just the perfect length for me since I almost use it's length fully because I at times like to sit my reclining chair maybe 1 foot away from my desk. However it's not too long such that there's cables hanging anywhere during normal use.

8. Overall looks great. Not too blocky but also not overdone. Has a general nice dark sleek look to it, which perfectly complements the RBG that'll be coming from the keys. I love how it looks from the side because of how mechanical keys are raised so the RBG bleeds out from under, not just through the key letter itself.

title: Yeah Baby, I Like It
text:
The XA40 and XA45 are the same except that the XA45 has an SDI port for more flexibility for output to external devices. If SDI output is important to you, it’s a no-brainer. Otherwise, get the XA40.

The first thing you should consider is the sensor size. In general, the larger the sensor, the better the low-light capability, and the shallower the depth of field. Also, cameras with smaller sensors tend to have longer optical zoom ranges, as is the case with the XA40/45. A good 20x to be exact.

Another thing you’ll want to consider is whether you need basic professional features, like XLR ports, ND filters, etc. The XA40/45 has these features, but as expected, more expensive models have better versions and even more professional features. The ND filter on the XA50/55 for example, is manually controlled, which in my opinion, is better.

Like just about all modern imaging devices, the 40/45 series comes with image stabilization. Don’t expect it to work well when you are walking. Sure, it’ll be steadier than without it, but my take is that the stabilization is really meant to steady your shots when you are hand-holding the camera and not walking. It might just be me, but when I walk with the camera, the bob in the footage is more pronounced than I would like.

If you’re comfortable with the 1/2.3 inch sensor in the 40/45, as opposed to a larger 1 inch sensor or bigger, and you’re not quite an enthusiast but want room to grow, you are in the right camp. If you do happen to be an enthusiast, this camera is still a good choice. Pros might want to look at the 50/55 series or higher (think XF line).

If you’re a beginner who has no desire to venture beyond full automatic, you can get the same quality for less money with the Vixia HF G50. It’ll give you the same results but with fewer professional options and a lower price tag.

There are a ton of features and specifications for the XA40/45, which you can look up at the Canon website, or better yet by downloading and reading the manual. Perhaps the most important thing that I can tell you, is that you can get great quality footage in full auto. You also have the option of to be more creative by learning to use the manual settings.

Take advantage of a good quality, XLR shotgun microphone to isolate/intensify the sound coming from your subject(s). This camera is ready to roll in that respect and it would be a shame not to take advantage of it.

The XA40/45 is compatible with the Canon GP-E2, which is a GPS receiver. For me, knowing where and when (yes, it can read the time off the satellites) is important.

The one drawback for me, is that unlike higher level models, the XA 40/45 is not compatible with the Canon WL-D89 wireless remote controller. I always want that option in a camcorder. This is not a flaw, but a "nice to have".

Finally, this series of camcorder records in MP4. Higher level models record in MP4 and XF-AVC. For the most part, it probably won’t make a difference. But if you want to push things, XF-AVC is a higher quality codec. For my purposes, it doesn’t make a difference – yet. Still, while it doesn’t make a difference for my shooting needs, I always shoot in the best available codec if I have the choice (as I do with my Canon XF400).

If I had to highlight what I like most about the XA40/45, it would be the 20x zoom, the ability to use a GPS, the relative simplicity of operation, the basic array of professional features, and the lens hood with flip cover. I leave the hood on all the time. Other than the fact that the hood is larger than the cap, it is much better than using the cap. Also, while I have camcorders with 1 inch sensors (and even bigger in my DSLRs), there is something to be said for the greater depth of field of smaller sensors.

I'm very pleased with this camcorder.
